# Applye Duty Watch

This file is the chronological handoff log for maintainers and AI agents working on Applye.

`docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md` remains the canonical operational state. This log records how each work session changed, verified, or failed to change that state.

Append new entries at the top under `## Watch Log`. Do not erase older entries to hide mistakes or incomplete work. Correct inaccurate entries with a later entry and repository evidence.

## Duty completion checklist

Before a watch can be marked complete:

- [ ] The final diff was reviewed.
- [ ] Relevant checks from `docs/governance/VALIDATION_MATRIX.md` were run.
- [ ] `npm run format:check` passed, or an unavailable formatter was reported honestly.
- [ ] `git diff --check` passed.
- [ ] `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md` was updated if focus, blockers, implementation status, or next action changed.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md`, roadmap, ADRs, specs, migrations, privacy, security, and design docs were updated when applicable.
- [ ] Any failed, skipped, unavailable, or manual-only checks are recorded.
- [ ] The next first action is concrete and executable.

## Entry template

```md
### YYYY-MM-DD, concise watch title

- **Status:** complete | partial | blocked | rolled back
- **Agent/tool:**
- **Branch:**
- **Commits:**
- **Pull request:**
- **Objective:**
- **Completed:**
- **Not completed:**
- **Files or packages changed:**
- **Validation:**
- **Privacy/security impact:**
- **Decisions and assumptions:**
- **Risks or compatibility impact:**
- **Open issues or blockers:**
- **Next first action:**
- **Evidence:**
```

- **Completed, in the order found:**
  1. **`#520`** - `TailoringService.restoreFromCache()` always hashed the cache lookup against
     `profile.fullMd`; the live run (`runPass()`) hashes against `baselineFor(ctx)` (the selected base
     CV when one is set). A job tailored against a chosen base CV showed "Tailor" instead of "Retailor"
     on reopen. Fixed by routing `restoreFromCache` through `baselineFor(ctx)` too.
  2. **`#521`** - a tailoring pass that failed mid-wizard (e.g. invalid AI JSON on pass 2) left no way
     forward: not the from-scratch picker, not the thinking row, not the tailored badge, just error
     text. Added a Retry button re-emitting `startTailoring`, which resumes from cache for the passes
     already done.
  3. **`#522`** - `#520` was the wrong-shaped fix. `CvDraftService.persist()` relinks `cvDocumentId` to
     its own tailored _output_ (`ADR-0003` row reuse), so `selectedBaseCvId` on reopen resolves to that
     output, not to whatever pass 1 actually hashed against - the cache miss recurred for essentially
     every job with an application. A "linked CV is AI-generated" heuristic was checked and rejected
     (`CvGenerateStore`'s unrelated one-shot generator writes the identical `source: 'generated'`).
     Grilled with the maintainer (`aif-grilling`, one round): fixed by tagging the pipeline's own output
     `source: 'tailored'` (a new `DocumentSource` union member, no migration - `source` is
     unconstrained `TEXT`) and reading `isTailored` from that tag as well as the live signal. Scope
     stayed badge/CTA only, not a full phase-card/Changes/Gaps restore on reopen - flagged as a
     separate, larger ask if ever wanted.
  4. **`#523`** - two more native reports, grilled together: (a) a score/rescore run reset to
     "Score this job" if the user left and returned to the page - `JobScoringService` is
     component-scoped and `jobs.component.ts` read its `running` signal directly instead of
     `WizardActivityService.isRunning`; fixed to mirror `tailoring`. (b) the Tailor wizard's Cancel
     button implied an instant stop it cannot do (`AiService.run()` has no request id or cancellation
     path in either API/`reqwest` or CLI/spawned-process mode). Grilled: real cancellation needs new
     Rust plumbing, out of scope; recommended and chosen the honest-copy fix instead
     ("Cancelling..." to "Finishing this pass...", a hint, all 6 locales).
  5. **`#524`** - clicking "Score this job" gave no visible feedback until the result appeared. Added
     the `ai-thinking` dots animation next to the button, matching the Tailor wizard's own pattern.
  6. **`#525`** - **`#523`'s scoring-persistence fix was itself wrong for the button it targeted.**
     `JobScoringService.score()` - what "Score this job" actually calls - never registered with
     `WizardActivityService` at all; only `rescoreAfterTailor()` (the wizard's post-tailor step) did.
     `#523` assumed both methods wrote to it, so the signal read `false` for the _entire_ `score()` run
     - a regression from the old (also wrong, but at least page-local-visible) flag. Native re-test
       confirmed: no animation, no disabled state. Fixed by adding the same `activity.begin`/`end` pair to
       `score()`. Also extended the shell's corner badge (`shell-layout.component.ts`) to a bare
       baseline score in flight - it was gated only on `WizardProgressService.progress()`, which a plain
       "Score this job" click before the apply wizard opens never sets. Grilled: a second copy key
       (`resume_bare_scoring_title`, "Scoring this job...") rather than reusing the wizard rescore's
       "Scoring your tailored CV...", wrong for a job nothing has tailored yet.
  7. **`#526`** - the `#524` dots landed as a second pill beside the button rather than inside it -
     "Scoring..." (disabled button) plus a separate floating "Scoring..." badge, same word twice.
     `ai-thinking__dots` is standalone by design for exactly this (`libs/ui/src/styles/global.scss`'s
     own comment: "so it also renders inside buttons"), and the Documents step's Generate/Regenerate
     buttons already use it that way. Moved the dots inside both buttons instead of a sibling element.
  - **Merge-conflict handling:** `#526` was branched before `#525` merged and both touched the top of

  own "next first action"; (2) pick and complete one item from the open backlog.
- **Completed:**
  - `#515` opened (later found auto/already merged by the time of push - `git branch --show-current`
    read `main` again at the session's start, matching this file's own recorded gotcha about the
    working tree resetting to `main` between sessions; the branch and its two commits were intact).
  - **Root cause of the raw-Cmd+P bug confirmed by reading, not assumed**: `tauri.invoke.ts`'s
    `isTauri()` guard and the print stylesheet in `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss` are both scoped to
    `body.printing-cv`, which `print-settle.util.ts` only ever sets inside the two hidden export-route
    windows (`markPrintPath()` + the class, both driven by `awaitPrintSettle()`). Neither `cv-detail`'s
    existing `beforeprint` handler (which only clears the live inline-selection, per its own comment)
    nor `cover-letter-detail` (which had no `beforeprint` handling at all) ever set it, so a raw
    Cmd/Ctrl+P opened the browser print dialog with the print stylesheet dark - the whole shell prints.
  - **Fact resolved before grilling, not asked**: `grep` across `src-tauri` found no native menu item
    or accelerator bound to Print, confirming Cmd+P is WKWebView's own default shortcut reaching the
    DOM as a normal `beforeprint`/`afterprint` pair - which is why "redirect to Export via keydown

### 2026-08-22, duplicate-heading print bug: root cause was fragmentation, not a margin gap

- **Status:** complete. Committed to the branch; PR not opened.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Sonnet 5 for most of the session (started under Opus 5, switched mid-session by the maintainer via `/model`). Triage printed three times: 7/10 at session start (radius 1, ambiguity 2, risk 1, verify 2, unknowns 1), re-triaged to 7/10 at close-out (radius 2, ambiguity 0, risk 1, verify 2, unknowns 0) once scope moved from verification to commit-and-document, then skipped as ceremony for the small follow-up correcting these docs after the maintainer's redesign decision. No subagents (none requested).
- **Branch:** `fix/paginated-sheet-print-fragmentation`, cut from `main` (working tree was on `main` at session start, per this file's own recorded gotcha - checked before assuming otherwise).
- **Commits:** `e695178f` - "fix(print): stop WKWebView fragmenting the next card into leftover page space".
- **Pull request:** not opened.
- **Objective:** the previous session's handoff (`docs/internal/NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md`) named two tasks: (1) confirm two uncommitted print-margin constants (`PRINT_WIDTH_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX = 4`, `PRINT_HEIGHT_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX` 16 to 24) against a genuinely clean, post-WebKit-cache-clear native export, since every prior "confirmation" had turned out contaminated; (2) decide, only after that, whether the pagination-timing redesign discussed and deferred last session was still needed.
- **Completed:**
  - **The WebKit cache alarm from the previous session was a false positive.** `~/Library/Caches/applye-desktop/WebKit/NetworkCache`'s parent directory mtime was stuck on 27 June because a directory's mtime only moves when its _direct_ children change, not its descendants - the `Version 17/` subdirectory inside it was current. Grepping the cached JS blob directly (`grep -o 'PRINT_HEIGHT_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX = [0-9]*'` against the binary cache file) confirmed the print window was loading the fixed constants throughout. No cache-staleness bug existed at the point this session picked the work up.
  - **The width margin's original justification (`0.9pt past the clip`) and the height margin's original justification (`2.02pt below the clip`) were both re-derived from scratch with a corrected forensic method, and one number changed.** A `pypdf` script (`/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/pdf_forensics.py`, not committed - lives in the session scratchpad) measures each text run's real end position from the font's own `/Widths` array against the page's own `re W n` clip rectangles. First pass overstated every width by 25%: WKWebView's print pass writes `Tf /F 1` and carries the real point size in the text matrix, then scales the whole page by `cm[0] = 0.8` (72pt / 90px-per-inch - WKWebView's print rasterizer runs at 90 DPI, not the 96 DPI the on-screen layout assumes), so a script using the text-matrix scale alone reports every width 25% too wide. Corrected, the width margin's justification held: `Oslo, Norway` on an export with the margin removed would end roughly 2.77pt past the clip edge. The height margin's justification did not hold as originally stated - see the disproof below.
  - **Root cause found for the duplicate-heading bug, replacing four sessions of margin-based patching.** Two native exports of the same CV at `PRINT_HEIGHT_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX = 24` (not the 16px the bug was first observed at) both showed "LANGUAGES" painted twice: once, clipped, in a small extra clip region below the first page-card's own box on page 1, and once whole at the top of page 2. Critically, the paginator's own page-break decision was already correct - page 2's clip is exactly one heading plus one line tall, meaning the atom had been assigned to the right page. The extra clip region on page 1 is WKWebView beginning to lay the _next_ page-card out in whatever printable space is left at the foot of the current page, painting its first line(s) into that leftover space, then honouring the forced page break afterward - so the heading is drawn once in the leftover strip and again on the next page. This means every previous margin increase had been _feeding_ the bug: more packing headroom means _less_ content per card, which means _more_ unused space at the foot of each page for WKWebView to fragment the next card into.
  - **Two alternate fixes were tried and measured to change nothing, before the real fix was found.** Swapping the page-break property from `break-before: page` (on `.page-card-wrap + .page-card-wrap`) to `break-after: page` (on `.page-card-wrap:not(:last-child)`) was grilled with the maintainer as the first candidate; `check-style-move.mjs` confirmed it as exactly one intentional selector swap; all gates passed; a fresh native export showed the exported PDF's clip geometry unchanged to the hundredth of a point. This proved the break property itself was never the lever - the leftover space exists regardless of which side of the boundary owns the break.
  - **The fix that measured clean:** every page-card but the last is now given the _exact_ printed page height, via a new `--pc-page-height` CSS custom property driven by a new `pageBoxHeightPx()` computed signal in `PaginatedSheetComponent` (`libs/ui/src/lib/paginated-sheet/paginated-sheet.ts`), applied in `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss` as `body.printing-cv .page-card-wrap:not(:last-child) .page-card { height: var(--pc-page-height) !important; }`. A card that fills its page exactly leaves no leftover space for WebKit to fragment the next card into. The last card deliberately keeps `height: auto` - giving it a full page too, with nothing following it, is exactly what produces a trailing blank page. `PRINT_HEIGHT_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX` (still 24) and `PRINT_WIDTH_SAFETY_MARGIN_PX` (still 4) both stay: their headroom is now interior to each full-height card, below its last atom, where nothing can be painted into it. `pageBoxHeightPx()` itself carries one more measured number: it trims 1px off the geometry's own page-height computation, because a live export's page content box read 728.00pt (910.00px at the 0.8 print scale) against a computed 910.63px - a 0.63px screen-vs-print rounding gap on top of the fragmentation bug, closed the same way `#511`'s width fix closed its own.
  - **Re-exporting the same CV after the CSS change confirmed the fix**, per the maintainer directly: the exported PDF now matches the in-app preview, with no duplicate heading and the leftover clip region gone. Page count unchanged at 2.
  - **Full commit gate set run and green on the branch**, `--skip-nx-cache` where the checklist calls for it: `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=data,application,desktop,ui --skip-nx-cache` (pass; one pre-existing, unrelated non-null-assertion warning in `cv-gap-dialog.component.spec.ts`), `nx run desktop:type-check` (pass), `nx run ui:type-check` (pass), `nx test data` (83/83), `nx test application` (1684/1684), `nx test ui` (37/37), `nx test desktop --maxWorkers=2` (1165/1165), `nx build desktop` (pass), `npm run quality:file-size -- --staged` (pass - the `--base main` form read "no changed source files" at first, the exact stale-comparison gotcha this file already records, since the branch had just been cut from `main` with no divergence yet), `npm run quality:attribution` (pass), `npm run format:check` (pass), `git diff --check` (clean). `libs/core` and `apps/desktop/src-tauri` were untouched this session, so their gates (`nx test core`, `nx build web`, `cargo check`, `cargo test --lib`) did not need to run.
  - `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md` rewritten (not merely appended to) to replace the previous, now-disproven entries describing the margin raise as the fix for the duplicate heading. Both now state the fragmentation mechanism, the two rejected fixes, and the confirmed result.
- **Not completed:** `B9`, `B5`, `S1`, the raw-Cmd+P print gap, and a native pass over the disabled-Retailor/locked-editor state (`P1`/`P2`/`B12`) were untouched this session - all four were already recorded open before this session started and none regressed. **The pagination-timing redesign question is resolved, not merely deferred again**: after the fix was confirmed and committed, the maintainer decided directly, in this same session, that the redesign is not needed - the failure mode that motivated it is closed at its source. This is a settled decision recorded here and in `docs/internal/NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md`, not an open item for the next session to re-evaluate.
- **Files or packages changed:** `libs/ui/src/lib/paginated-sheet/paginated-sheet.ts` (new `pageBoxHeightPx()` and `PRINT_PAGE_BOX_TRIM_PX`; corrected comments on the two existing margin constants), `libs/ui/src/lib/paginated-sheet/paginated-sheet.html` (new `--pc-page-height` binding), `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss` (the `break-before`→`break-after` swap, later superseded by the `--pc-page-height` fix; both changes are in the diff, since the break-property swap remains harmless and the CSS comment explains why it was tried and rejected), `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** see the gate list above; all observed directly, none assumed. Native validation was two real exports of the maintainer's own stored CV content (not synthetic or hand-edited test data), read forensically with `pypdf` and confirmed against the in-app preview by the maintainer directly in WPS Office and Applye's own preview pane.

### 2026-08-21, one document, one export path

- **Status:** complete. The second export path is closed; `B4`'s remaining gap is now a single block between preview and file, which the next export will measure.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage **7/10**. The decision had already been taken in an earlier round and the maintainer proposed it again in their own words, so no fresh gate. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `fix/one-export-path`, cut from `origin/main` at `a6474b95`.

- **The measurement that justified it, from the maintainer's own pair of exports:** the same document, the same margins, two buttons.
  - editor's Export: clip `0 0 595 841` - **the whole sheet, no margins at all**;
  - Documents list: clip `56.69 56.69 481 728` - **20mm, correct**.
- **The cause is structural, not a bug in either button.** `window.print()` raises the macOS dialog, and that dialog owns its own `NSPrintInfo`. The Style card's margins have no route into it. No amount of CSS could have fixed that path, which is why it kept reporting the defect after the CSS was already right.
- **Both editors now save, then call the same export the Documents list uses.** One path, driven from Rust with the document's own page settings.
- **Saving first is the part that needed thought.** The hidden window renders the **stored** document, so an unsaved edit would be missing from the file. `cv-detail.component.ts` deliberately does not persist a half-typed draft on a raw Cmd+P, and that rule is untouched: the user did not ask for a write there. Pressing Export **is** asking for this document to become a file, and a file of something other than what was asked for is worse than a save the user did not name. The reasoning is written above the method, not in a commit message.
- **`printWithPageRule` and `pageRuleFor` are deleted.** Nothing called them once both editors moved; `wysiwyg-print.ts` goes from 132 to 56 lines and keeps only `markPrintPath`, which the export windows still need.
- **Found while removing them, recorded and not fixed:** a raw Cmd+P in either editor sets no `printing-cv` class and injects no page rule, so it prints the **whole application**. That was already true - the Export button was the only thing that ever set the class - so it is not a regression, and it is a defect of its own rather than a rider on this change.

- **Three specs changed rather than deleted**, and each says why in its own comment: the CV editor's export test now asserts that it does **not** print, the cover letter's likewise, and the print-protocol spec keeps only what survives. They are tripwires: a well-meant `window.print()` put back on either path restores a second export that answers differently from the first, which is the defect rather than the mechanism.
- **The desktop suite failed once with `Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms` and no assertion failing.** That is the shape `PR #487` measured and named: nine jest workers on a loaded machine, and the machine was running the maintainer's Tauri dev server and a PDF viewer. Re-run at `--maxWorkers=2`: **1160 passed**. Checked the load before the code, as the log says to.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=core,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with pre-existing warnings only; `nx test desktop` **1160 passed**, `nx test core` **478 passed**; `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.65 kB; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none.
- **Next first action:** export a two-page CV from either button and compare the break with the editor - they should now break in the same place and produce the same file. Then `P1`/`P2`/`B12`, which has been specified and waiting for several rounds.

- **The maintainer supplied the artefact that ended it**: the same CV exported twice, once with 20mm margins and once with all four set to zero. That pair is what no amount of code reading could substitute for.
  - clip boxes: `56.69 56.69 481 728` and `0 0 595 841` - `NSPrintInfo` doing exactly what it is told. **The margins were never the problem.**
  - text-matrix scale: `0.8000236` and `0.8008075`. **A tenth of a percent apart while the printable box changed by 40mm in each direction.** That is the whole diagnosis: a fixed CSS-px-to-point mapping, not a shrink-to-fit. WKWebView prints 0.8pt per px - 90 to the inch.
- **The previews used `96 / 25.4`**, the display convention and the obvious choice, which models every page **6.67% larger than the sheet**. Both symptoms follow from that one ratio: the measured column is 642.5px where the printable area is 602, so text wraps differently in the export; and the paginator packs 971.3px into a card where 910.75px can print, so the remainder is **clipped**.
- **The export was losing text, not mis-margining it.** On the 20mm file the last text baseline is at `y = 47.07` with the clip floor at `56.69` - drawn below the visible box. That reframes `B4` from cosmetic to data-losing, and it is why the page breaks never matched the editor no matter what happened to the margins.
- **`PRINT_PX_PER_MM = 72 / 25.4 / 0.8`** lives in `libs/core/src/lib/cv/cv-page.util.ts` with the measurement written above it, and both previews use it. An A4 sheet maps to 595.3 x 841.9pt, and the column and usable height come out at 602.0 x 910.7px - the numbers the clip box carries.
- **Measured on macOS**, the only platform with a print path today (`macos_print_to_pdf`). A webview mapping pixels to points differently would need this per-platform; the constant's comment says how to re-measure it from an exported file, which is the part that makes the number maintainable rather than magic.

- **Why four attempts missed it, recorded because the pattern is the lesson.** Every one moved the margins between layers, because the margins were what the eye noticed - and they had been correct since the second attempt. The wrong thing was never a margin; it was **the size of the page the preview believed in**, which no symptom named until the exports were compared side by side. Reading code cannot find a number that is only visible in the output.
- **Files changed:** `libs/core/src/lib/cv/cv-page.util.ts` and a new `print-scale.spec.ts`, both preview components and their specs.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=core,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with pre-existing warnings only; `nx test core` **478 passed**, six new; `nx test desktop` **1169 passed**; `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.66 kB; `nx build web` green, run because `libs/core` changed; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed.
- **What the new tests claim:** they pin the two measured numbers against the printable boxes the real exports carry - the column at 481.6pt, the usable height at 728.6pt, a whole A4 sheet at 595.3 x 841.9pt, and the 96/90 ratio that clipped the export. They are evidence transcribed, not arithmetic restated.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none.
- **Next first action:** export a two-page CV from the Documents list and compare the page break with the editor - they should break in the same place, and no text should be missing from the end of page one. Then `P1`/`P2`/`B12`.

### 2026-08-21, the margins were applied twice, and the second place was Rust

- **Status:** complete for the half that can be fixed in one change. The editor's own Export button is a second path, specified and not implemented.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage **9/10**, budget announced. Grilling gate ran once, after the analysis rather than before it - the fork only appeared once the cause was known. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `fix/print-margins-belong-to-the-print-system`, cut from `origin/main` at `ba31f9a9`.

- **The maintainer asked the question that ended it: "why did this work before?"** Three attempts had each been an honest reading of the evidence then available, and all three had moved the margins between two CSS layers. **There is a third.** `export_pdf_wysiwyg_core` in `commands/print.rs` reads the document's page settings and puts them on `NSPrintInfo` - `setTopMargin`, `setRightMargin`, `setBottomMargin`, `setLeftMargin`. The print system insets the page before any CSS is consulted, so a `@page` margin is the same millimetres a second time.
- **The arithmetic matches the exports, which is what makes this diagnosis different from the previous three.** A4 with 20mm margins is a 257mm content box = the 971px `paginate.util.ts` packs a card into. Applied twice: 217mm, 820px, **151px short** - and the four or five displaced atoms are exactly what appeared at the top of exported page two while the preview kept them on page one.
- **"It worked before the refactor" is a true memory of a different thing.** Both halves arrived in the same commit, `eb431567` on 2026-07-15, so this path has never produced correct margins. `#466`, the print-protocol refactor the maintainer remembered, moved the code without changing it - verified by reading its diff. No export had been measured against the Style card until the walk of 2026-08-20.
- **None of the three attempts was the right configuration**, and the shape is worth keeping: original was `@page` margins + card padding 0 (twice); the first fix was `@page` 0 + card padding (a card exactly one page tall, page two flush); the second and third went back to `@page` margins (twice again). The correct one is **`@page` 0 + card padding 0**, which nobody had tried.

- **What this change does and does not fix.** It makes the **save-to-file** export exact, because `NSPrintInfo` carries the document's own margins there. **The editor's Export button is a second path**: it calls `window.print()`, so its `NSPrintInfo` comes from the macOS dialog's defaults and the Style card's margins cannot reach it at all.
- **The maintainer chose to route that button through the same Rust export the Documents list uses**, which makes both paths exact and leaves one print path instead of two. It is deliberately **not** in this change: it replaces a print dialog with a save dialog, and the Rust path renders the **saved** document, so the editor must persist before exporting - and `cv-detail.component.ts` deliberately does not persist a half-typed draft on a raw Cmd+P, a rule the new path must not break.

- **Files changed:** `wysiwyg-print.ts` and its spec, `cv-detail.style.spec.ts`, plus documents. No stylesheet: the card already carries `padding: 0` in print, so the CSS half needed only the `@page` rule.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning; `nx test desktop` **1169 passed**; `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.82 kB; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed.
- **What to test next is a different button**: the Documents list's **Export PDF**, not the editor's. That is the path this change makes exact, and testing the editor's would report the same defect for a reason this change does not address.
- **The lesson, recorded because it cost four rounds.** Every attempt reasoned inside one layer - CSS - because that is where the symptom was visible. The margins had three owners and the third was in another language, in another process boundary. **When a value can be applied by more than one layer, count the layers before choosing which one to change.**
- **Next first action:** route the editor's Export through the Rust path, with the save question decided; then `P1`/`P2`/`B12`.

### 2026-08-21, hiding is not removing

- **Status:** complete as a change. `B4`'s **third** attempt, and the third that this repository cannot verify. Owed a native pass on both pages of a two-page CV.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage **7/10** (radius 1, ambiguity 1, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 0 - the cause was named by the symptom). No grilling: one honest reading. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `fix/print-hides-siblings-from-layout`, cut from `origin/main` at `35da378e`.

- **The symptom named the cause, which is why this round did not need a decision.** The maintainer rebuilt with the previous fix and reported that **page one's top inset was larger than the Style card asks for**. An inset larger than the page margin is a flow that starts lower than the page area, and there is only one thing in this print path that can do that.
- **`visibility: hidden` reveals without reclaiming.** The property is _defined_ to preserve layout. The print stylesheet hid the whole application that way and made the sheet visible again, so every hidden sibling above the sheet kept its full height. **This was harmless for as long as the sheet was pinned** with `position: absolute`, because a pinned box is out of flow - and the previous fix, which unclipped the flow so `@page` margins could reach every page, is exactly what made the borrowed height real. One fix uncovered the other; the earlier entry had already named this hole and declined to patch it blind while the build question was open, which turned out to be the right call for a different reason than expected.
- **`display: none` removes a box, and the ancestors must be spared.** The CSS way to say that is `:has()`, and it **fails in the wrong direction**: an engine that does not understand the selector drops the whole rule and prints the entire application. `markPrintPath` in `wysiwyg-print.ts` walks from the sheet up to `<body>` marking each ancestor instead - deterministic, no selector support required, and **assertable in jsdom**, which none of the layout behind this bug is.
- **Both print paths mark**: the editor's `printWithPageRule`, which un-marks on `afterprint`, and `awaitPrintSettle` for the silent export windows, which deliberately does not - that window is opened to be snapshotted and closed, so there is no "after", and an un-mark racing the snapshot could blank the export.
- **The `visibility` pair stays underneath as the floor.** If the marking ever fails to run, the page is hidden rather than printed: the old bug rather than a much louder new one.

- **Files changed:** `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss`, `wysiwyg-print.ts` and its spec, `print-settle.util.ts`, plus documents.
- **`check-style-move.mjs`: 0 lost, 2 gained** - the two `display: none` rules and nothing else.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning; `nx test desktop` **1169 passed**, five new; `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.85 kB; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed.
- **What the five new tests claim**, and it is worth being exact because the last two rounds over-claimed: they assert that every ancestor up to `<body>` is marked, that **no sibling and not the sheet** is marked, that the undo restores the document, that **nothing is marked when there is no sheet**, and that the editor's print marks and un-marks around `window.print()`. They say nothing about the printed page, which has no layout in jsdom.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none.
- **Three attempts on one defect is worth recording as a pattern, not an apology.** Each was rejected by a native pass and each rejection named the next cause: page one lost its margins (pinning), page two lost its inset (a page-tall card cannot carry margins as padding), page one gained too much inset (hidden siblings keep their height). The repository could not have distinguished any of them; the maintainer's exports could, and did, in three rounds of a few minutes each.
- **Next first action:** the export, on **both** pages of a two-page CV. Then `P1`/`P2`/`B12`, which is specified and waiting.

### 2026-08-21, the first native pass on four unseen fixes, and one of them was wrong

- **Status:** complete. **Three of the four fixes are confirmed by the maintainer's own pass; the fourth was rejected and is re-fixed here**, differently, and is owed another pass.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. The maintainer ran the app; the agent read the evidence and changed the code. Triage **8/10** on the re-fix (radius 2, ambiguity 2, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 1); grilling gate ran once, one question. No subagents.

- **What the pass settled**, and it is the first time in this sequence that "fixed" and "seen" are the same word:
  - **`B2` passes.** All six disclosures opened and closed twice.
  - **`B6` passes.** A one-page tracker report exports as one page.
  - **`B10`** - the spinner - was covered by the same session.
  - **`B4` fails, and differently from before.** Page one came back correct. **Page two lost its inset.**

- **The rejected fix was wrong for a reason that is dimensional, not incidental**, which is worth stating because it is what makes the second attempt trustworthy. `paginate.util.ts` packs content into `pageHeightPx - marginTop - marginBottom`, so a card carrying the margins as **padding** is **exactly one page tall** whatever else is true of it. Printed onto a sheet whose printable area is smaller than the paper by any amount, it overflows, and `break-inside: avoid` moves a whole section down - onto a page with no top inset, because **padding belongs to a box and a margin belongs to every page it spans**. The maintainer's print preview showed `EDUCATION` and the bullet above it displaced off page one and flush at the paper edge, where the on-screen preview had page one ending with `EDUCATION`.

- **What was actually wrong all along was the pinning, and it is removed at its cause.** The sheet was `position: absolute` because `.shell` is `height: 100vh; overflow: hidden`, `.main` is `overflow: hidden`, and `.content` is the scrolling box - three clips a flowed sheet cannot escape. The print rules unclip all three and drop the sidebar and topbar with `display: none` rather than `visibility: hidden`, the same distinction `B6` turned on. The sheet is an ordinary block at the top of the document now, `@page` owns the margins again, and they repeat per page.

The code is doing what it was written to do, so it needs a decision and not a patch.

- **Files changed:** `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss`, `wysiwyg-print.ts` and its spec, `cv-detail.style.spec.ts`, plus documents.
- **`check-style-move.mjs` reports 1 selector losing declarations and 7 gaining**, all deliberate: the sheet loses its pinning, and the shell containers, the sidebar, the topbar and the card gain the rules above.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning; `nx test desktop` **1164 passed**; `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.85 kB; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed.

### 2026-08-21, the disclosure that WebKit would not re-open

- **Status:** complete as a code change. **Unverified as a fix**, and that is not a caveat on this entry - it is the defining fact about `B2` and it is stated in the partial, the spec, the changelog and the pull request.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage **7/10** (radius 1, ambiguity 2, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 1); the grilling gate ran on the ambiguity, one round, two questions. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `fix/disclosure-collapse-webkit`, cut from `origin/main` at `93a69cf2`.
- **Commits:** `ba964b77` (the fix and its documents), plus this line recording it. **The branch was cut from the `S1` documentation branch rather than from `main`**, so once #498 squash-merged it carried that work twice and GitHub reported a conflict against a change already on `main`. Repaired with `git rebase --onto origin/main <the duplicated commit>`, which replays only the two `B2` commits; the diff against `main` is now the six files below and nothing else, and every gate was re-run after it.
- **Objective:** `B2` from `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md`, the next item after `S1` was blocked on a measurement.

- **The bug.** `.docedit-collapse` animated `grid-template-rows` between `0fr` and `1fr`. WKWebView does not honour that transition: the section collapsed on the first click and never came back, entries still in the DOM at zero height, chevron open over nothing. Tauri renders in WKWebView on macOS; jsdom and Chrome both accept the construction, which is why it shipped.
- **The replacement is chosen for how it fails.** `height: 0` to `height: auto` with `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`. Block layout with a height is what every engine has implemented for decades, so the control is correct even where nothing animates, and `interpolate-size` lets engines that can animate to a keyword ease it. **The old technique degraded into a broken control on one engine; this one degrades into an unanimated one.** That property, rather than the animation quality, is what decided it.
- **`display: grid` is gone with the `fr` units it existed for.** Checked rather than assumed: all six call sites wrap their content in exactly one child, so the container was a single-item grid.
- **The walk's narrowing was checked and did not change the fix.** The walk recorded "the Style card re-opens correctly", which would point at the markup rather than the rule. Both markups are structurally identical - `.docedit-collapse > div > content` - so the difference is the content: the CV sections hold component hosts with their own editors, the Style card holds plain fields. One disclosure happening not to break is weaker evidence than the technique being unreliable in the engine, and the finding's own instruction was to fix once in the partial. Six disclosures change: the CV section accordion, both Style cards, and the cover letter's blocks, body paragraphs and recipient block.
- **`interpolate-size` is declared on the element rather than on `:root`.** It is inherited, so a global declaration would quietly enable keyword interpolation for every other transition in the app.
- **The child's `overflow: hidden` is kept although the container now clips.** Removing it would let content that is currently clipped escape - a second visual change riding along with a bug fix, in the one place no test here can see it.

- **What the new spec does and does not claim.** `apps/desktop/src/disclosure-css.spec.ts` scans the partial's declarations and fails if an `fr`-unit track transition returns, if the closed state stops clipping, if `interpolate-size` goes global, or if reduced motion is dropped. It follows `cv-print-css.spec.ts` and `followup-no-transmit.spec.ts`, the existing pattern for rules no fixture can reach. **It is a guard on the technique, not evidence about the behaviour** - jsdom has no layout and the engine that broke is not in this repository. The spec's own header says so, so a later reader cannot mistake a green suite for a verified fix. **The first version of it failed on its own explanation**: the comments name `:root` and `grid-template-rows`, so a scan of the raw file matched the prose; every assertion now runs against the declarations with comment lines stripped.
- **The design hook objected, and it was left unchanged deliberately.** `impeccable` flags animating `height` and recommends `grid-template-rows` for height animations - which is the exact construction being removed. Classified as a false positive in this context rather than silenced: no inline disable, no config ignore, and the reason is written into the partial where the next person to see the warning will read it.

- **Files changed:** `apps/desktop/src/app/pages/documents/editor-shell/_disclosure.scss` (34 to 68 lines, mostly the reasoning) and the new `apps/desktop/src/disclosure-css.spec.ts`. No template, no TypeScript, no Rust.
- **`check-style-move.mjs` was run, as it must be when a stylesheet changes, and it reports a real delta rather than a move**: `.docedit-collapse` loses `display: grid`, `grid-template-rows: 1fr` and its transition, `.docedit-collapse--closed` loses `grid-template-rows: 0fr`, and the two gain the height mechanism. That is the intended change and the pull request names it, which is what the tool asks for.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=data,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning; `nx test desktop` **1153 passed** (five new); `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.72 kB, no budget warning; `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed. No Rust, `libs/core`, `libs/data` or `libs/application` change, so their targets do not apply.
- **Not covered by anything here, and this is the whole point of the item:** whether the section re-opens. Station 4 settles it, and the other five disclosures should be opened and closed twice each on the same pass, because they now share the changed rule.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. One stylesheet.
- **Found while fixing, recorded rather than fixed:** closed content stays in the tab order. `overflow: hidden` hides it visually and leaves it focusable, so a keyboard user tabs into a collapsed section. True of the `fr` version too, so not a regression - a separate defect needing `inert` or `aria-hidden` across six templates rather than one rule. It is in `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md` under `B2`.
- **Next first action:** the print family `B4` `B5` `B6`, unless `S1`'s token numbers arrive first - `S1` is blocked on one query against `tailoring_cache`, not on a decision.

### 2026-08-20, the job title that was never truncated

- **Status:** complete as a fix to the deterministic extractor. **Not confirmed on the posting that reported it** - that needs a native re-parse, and the entry says so where it matters.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage **8/10** (radius 1, ambiguity 2, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 2). Ambiguity 2 sent it through the grilling gate before any edit: one round, three questions. No subagents.
- **Commits:** `7b12d2ec` (the fix and its documents), plus this line recording it.
- **Branch:** `fix/job-title-from-identify`, cut from `origin/main` at `11ea12a4` - `B11` (PR #496) already merged, so this branch starts from both previous fixes.
- **Objective:** `B8` from `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md`, third in the fix order. The title feeds the archetype screen, the score and the tailoring prompt, so a wrong one is read three times.

- **The premise in the finding's own title is wrong, and finding that out was most of the work.** Nothing truncated anything. A scanned posting is hard-wrapped at about eighty columns, so a fragment of a sentence **is** a line of the document, and `extract_title` takes the first body line under 80 characters that is not a section heading and carries a role word. **The reported fragment is 79 characters** - one under the cut. That is not a coincidence to leave unremarked: it is the longest string the filter permits, which is why it and not some other line.
- **It qualified on one word.** `ROLE_WORDS` was a list of role nouns with thirteen domain words mixed into it - `frontend`, `backend`, `fullstack`, `mobile`, `android`, `ios`, `web`, `data`, `product`, `project`, `sales`, `support`, `security` - each of them ordinary English that appears in the prose of a posting constantly. `frontend` was the entire reason that sentence became a job title.

- **Decisions taken through the grilling gate:**
  1. **Reject by sentence shape, not by tightening the length cut.** Lowering 80 to 55 would have fixed this posting and not the class: a 50-character prose fragment with `data` in it still passes. Five independent signals instead - a trailing full stop, a quoted percentage, an opener no title uses, more than ten words, and a sentence ending and another starting on one line. **The reported fragment is caught by three of them plus the role-word rule**, so the fix does not hang on any single rule being right about every posting in the world.
  2. **The thirteen domain words are demoted out of `ROLE_WORDS` rather than kept as a second tier.** Once the positional pass requires a role noun, a "qualifier" tier has nothing to do - `Frontend Engineer` already passes on `engineer`. Two tests carry the rule in both directions: one walks all thirteen and asserts none qualifies a line alone, the other walks the same words inside real titles and asserts every one still passes. The second is the one that would catch a well-meant re-addition.
  3. **The labelled pass is untouched.** `Job title: ...` states what its value is; position is the only evidence the second pass has, and it is the pass that needs the strictness. A test pins the exemption with a labelled line that every prose rule would otherwise reject.
  4. **Source precedence is left alone, and the cost is recorded rather than hidden.** A wrong deterministic title is still permanent: `job-identity-resolver.service.ts` fills a title only when it is empty (`job.title || identified.title`), so the AI never gets a turn to correct one. Making a positional guess a weaker provenance the AI may overwrite would add a value to a stored column and an AI call to parses that currently make none - its own decision, not a rider on this one.
  5. **No ADR.** Text rules, no layer movement.

- **Why strictness was the cheap lever, and it was checked rather than assumed.** Returning `None` is already a fully supported outcome - two existing tests assert it - and what follows it is the `job-identify` call and then the identity dialog. So refusing a doubtful line costs a placeholder and an economy-model call, while accepting a wrong one is presented as fact and reaches three consumers.
- **Abbreviations were the trap in rule 5 and are handled by word count.** `Sr. Engineer` and `Dipl.-Ing. Maschinenbau Manager` are titles, and a naive "full stop then a capital" test rejects both. The rule applies only above five words. `iOS Developer` was the trap in rule 3: a bare is-the-first-letter-lowercase test rejects it, so the rule tests the first **word** against a list of openers no title uses instead.

- **Files changed:** `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/job_identity.rs` only, plus documents. Source **395 to 467/500**, tests 158 to 256/600. It passes, but the headroom is now thin: **the next change to this file should pay for itself by extracting the title rules** rather than adding to them, and doing that here would have mixed a refactor into a fix.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `cargo test --lib` **378 passed, 1 ignored** (46 in `job_identity`, of which 13 are new), `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean, `cargo check` green. `nx run desktop:type-check` green. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=data,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning. `nx test desktop` **1148**. `nx build desktop` green, 1.51 MB / 280.71 kB. `quality:file-size --staged` passed, reporting `job_identity.rs` at 467/500 against base 395. `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` passed. No TypeScript changed, so `nx test core/application/data` and `nx build web` do not apply.
- **Not covered by any check here:** the posting that reported it. The unit tests pin the rule, including the reported fragment verbatim, but whether the chain then produces a **right** title depends on `job-identify` and the dialog, and only a native re-parse of a hard-wrapped listing shows that.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. Pure text rules, no storage, no network, no new data.
- **Next first action:** `S1` - two and a half minutes to a first document, half of it in the dual critique. Measure first: whether the critique needs two passes at full document length, whether it can run against a diff, and whether it can overlap the build. The timings are already in `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md`; do not re-measure what is written down, extend it.

### 2026-08-20, the cover letter that fails on the first attempt can finally say why

- **Status:** complete as instrumentation and as a defect fix. **`B11` itself is not proven fixed**, and the entry below says so in every place it could be misread.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Re-triage scored **8/10** (radius 2, ambiguity 2, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 1) after the first read showed a Tauri IPC contract change; the grilling gate ran on the ambiguity, two rounds, five questions. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `fix/cover-letter-parse-and-stop-reason`, cut from `origin/main` at `8ea5ed4b` and **rebased onto `7fdf1340`** once `B1` merged as PR #495. The two share no source file; the conflict was the three append-at-the-top documents that always conflict here - `CHANGELOG.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md` and this log - and both sides were kept, newest first. Every gate below was re-run **after** the rebase, because green before a rebase says nothing about after it.
- **Commits:** `32407e6b` (the fix and its documents), plus this line recording it.
- **Objective:** `B11` from `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md`, second in the fix order. The plan's instruction was explicit and was followed: **capture the provider error on the failed attempt before theorising.**

- **The constraint, stated first because it shapes everything else:** `B11` cannot be reproduced without a real provider call, so nothing here proves the cause. What was deliverable was making the next occurrence diagnosable, and closing the defect found while looking.
- **One feature carried three strictnesses of parse, and the failing button sat on the weakest.** `parseCvSkillResponse` cleans, parses, and **repairs a truncated answer** before giving up. `parseCoverLetterResponse` - the editor's path - parses and rejects an array or a bare scalar, but does not repair. The wizard's **Generate cover letter** did neither: a raw `JSON.parse(cleanJsonText(...))` with a cast, as did **tailor an existing letter**. That ordering is the entire content of the walk's note that "CV generation on the same run did not do this".
- **The message the user saw could not distinguish the three causes the findings file says decide the fix.** `JSON.parse` throws `Unexpected end of JSON input` and nothing else - not the answer it choked on - and `DocumentReviewStatusService.fail` renders exactly that string. A timeout, a truncated response and a schema rejection were one sentence.
- **Both providers already report why they stopped, into a field the app discarded.** Anthropic's `stop_reason` and the OpenAI-compatible `finish_reason` sit in the same JSON body `ai/api.rs` already parses for `usage`. `AiResponse` carries it now. **Absent on the CLI bridge rather than invented** - a bridge that reports nothing must not be made to say "finished cleanly", because that is the one claim that would clear a truncation suspicion falsely.

- **Decisions taken through the grilling gate, and what each costs:**
  1. **Harden, do not repair.** Both draft paths use `parseCoverLetterResponse`. A truncated letter is still a failure, unlike a truncated CV: a CV's sections are visibly listed so a short one announces itself, while a letter reads as continuous prose and a repair would present missing paragraphs as a finished document.
  2. **The sibling raw cast in `cover-letter-tailor.service.ts` is fixed in the same change.** Two casts are one defect written twice, and the tailor path overwrites an existing letter, so a silent empty result there costs more.
  3. **`stopReason` is optional and additive** on the Tauri IPC contract. `isTruncatedStopReason` in `libs/core` is the single place that knows the two vendor spellings; the value is passed through Rust verbatim rather than normalised there, so the vendor knowledge sits next to the code that reads it.
  4. **The stop reason explains a failure and does not overrule a success.** A capped answer that parses is kept, which is what the CV path does today - the two stop diverging rather than diverging in a new direction. The cost is named: a letter cut off at a paragraph boundary is still saved silently short, and that may be what the reporter meant by "cuts off".
  5. **No ADR.** Nothing about the layering changes; the reasoning lives in the findings entry, the changelog and here.

- **One thing was found that nobody was looking for, and it is the reason the type-check refused the change.** The cast was hiding **missing required fields**: six of `CoverLetterContent`'s are required, and a partial answer was stored with `address: undefined` under a type that promised an object. The draft now spreads over `emptyCoverLetterContent()` - the editor store's own private empty letter, hoisted into `libs/core` rather than copied - so `CoverLetterContentStore` lost its duplicate in the same change.
- **The orphaned import is why `--skip-nx-cache` is mandatory on lint.** Removing `cleanJsonText` from the tailor service left `CoverLetterContent` unused, and the type-check was green with it there. That is the sixth time in this repository's log.

- **Files changed:** Rust - `ai/mod.rs` (`stop_reason` on `AiResponse`), `ai/api.rs` **236 to 306/400** (two readers, one shared helper, four tests), `ai/cli.rs` **420 to 424/500** (`None`, with the reason). TypeScript - new `libs/core/src/lib/ai/stop-reason.ts` (**30**) and spec (**29**); `cover-letter-content.model.ts` 118 to **144**; `cv-parse.util.ts` 270 to **279/400**; `libs/data/.../ai.service.ts`; new `libs/application/src/lib/documents/cover-letter-response.ts` (**51/250**) and spec (**76/600**); `cover-letter-draft.service.ts` 174, `cover-letter-tailor.service.ts` 206, `cover-letter-content.store.ts` 137 to **122**; both barrels. The budget script names two files as it always does for a growing file - `ai/cli.rs` at 424/500 and `cover-letter-tailor.service.ts` at 206/250 - and both passed; nothing else is close.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `cargo check` and `cargo test --lib` in `src-tauri` - **365 passed, 1 ignored**, including four new tests covering both providers' spellings, a clean stop, and a missing/null/blank reason. `nx run desktop:type-check` green. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=core,data,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green after the two fixes above, with only pre-existing warnings. `nx test core` **472**, `nx test application` **1652**, `nx test desktop` **1148**, `nx test data` **83**. `nx build desktop` green, 1.50 MB / 280.38 kB. `nx build web` green - run because `libs/core` changed, though the web app imports nothing from it. `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` all passed.
- **Not covered by any check here:** whether `B11` is gone. The next native run should read the message on a failed first attempt; it will now name the cause, and the two answers point at different fixes - a token cap means the cap or the prompt, a clean stop means the skill is returning something that is not the JSON asked for.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none, and one thing checked rather than assumed. The parse error carries the first 200 characters of the **model's answer** - the letter being written for the user, shown to that user, never leaving the machine - which is what `parseCvSkillResponse` and `parseCoverLetterResponse` already did. `stop_reason` is a provider status word. No key, prompt or profile text is added to any message.

### 2026-08-20, a cancelled re-tailor stopped destroying the tailoring before it

- **Status:** complete for `B1`. Two other native-gate items it touched are unchanged and stated below.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. Triage scored the task **6/10** (radius 1, ambiguity 1, risk 1, verification 2, unknowns 1), which routes to Sonnet at high effort; the session ran on Opus and that mismatch is recorded rather than corrected, because the model is not the session's to switch. No subagents were spawned.
- **Branch:** `fix/tailoring-discard-owns-its-pass`, cut from `origin/main` at `8ea5ed4b`.
- **Commits:** `c042e659` (the fix and its documents), plus this line recording it.
- **Objective:** `B1` from `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md` - the first item in the fix order, and the only defect in that file that costs the user tokens on every occurrence.
- **The grilling gate ran before any edit**, because scoping the deletion changes what a `libs/application` service may destroy. Two rounds, four questions, and the facts each round needed were settled by reading rather than asked: that `document_library_delete` unlinks and then deletes, so the loss was permanent; that `enterJob` cannot re-read a route that still points at the id it loaded; that `TailorScoreService` holds only the in-memory post-tailor rescore; that `WizardProgressService` had already settled `sessionStorage` in this layer under `ADR-0005` amendment thirty-three; and that there are **two** wizard-open paths but only **one** draft-creation path, which is what chose the mechanism.

- **One symptom, two defects, and the cheap one is what made the expensive one look survivable.**
  1. **The screen.** `JobActionsStore.discardTailoring` called `resetJobScopedState()` and stopped. The route param has not changed, so `enterJob` treats the job as already loaded and re-reads nothing: the detail rendered blank and only recovered by leaving for My Jobs and coming back. It awaits `lifecycle.loadJob(id)` now, which the sibling `updateApplication` was already doing. **This is why the score appeared to be gone** - the baseline in `scoring_cache` was never touched, so no write was needed to bring it back.
  2. **The documents.** `TailoringDiscardService` deleted every linked document with `isApplicationDraft` set. That reads as safe, because a committed document is excluded - but `ADR-0003` deliberately leaves a tailored job's documents in draft until the user exports them or marks the job applied, so a job tailored once and re-tailored had **both passes' documents in draft**, and cancelling the second deleted the first's. Permanently.

- **Ownership is recorded where a draft is born, not snapshotted when the wizard opens.** `TailoringPassDraftsService` records a library row as the pass's inside `JobDocumentDraftsStore.link`, and the discard may destroy nothing outside that record. The alternative - snapshot the linked drafts at wizard open, delete what is not in the snapshot - gives the same answer for `B1` and has the wrong failure mode: there are two open paths (`openWizard` and the cross-job confirm) and a snapshot missed on either silently restores the old behaviour. There is one creation path, and it cannot be routed around.
- **The record is session-scoped on purpose, and so is what happens when it is empty.** `sessionStorage`, because the discard service is component-scoped and an in-memory record would be lost the moment the user steps into the document editor - which would widen the next discard back out to everything. After an app restart the record is empty and a discard therefore deletes **nothing**. An orphaned draft is a row the user can delete; a destroyed one cost tokens and is gone.
- **Every way a pass ends now disowns its drafts** - closing the wizard, marking applied, updating the application, and the discard itself, the last of these only after its deletes are through so a failed discard can still be retried by something that has the authority to finish.

- **Files changed:** `libs/application/src/lib/jobs/tailoring-pass-drafts.service.ts` (new, **81/250**) and its spec (**67/600**); `tailoring-discard.service.ts` 88 to **105/250**, spec 152 to **162/600**; `job-actions.store.ts` 183 to **187/250**, spec 258 to **285/600**; `job-document-drafts.store.ts` 186 to **185/250**; `libs/application/src/index.ts`. Docs: `ADR-0003` gains amendment one, plus `NATIVE_GATE_FINDINGS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`. **Nothing is near a budget**; counts are non-empty lines, as the budget script counts them.
- **Validation, all run and observed:** `nx run desktop:type-check` green; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=data,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` green with the one pre-existing warning in `cv-gap-dialog.component.spec.ts:68` (a file this branch does not touch); `nx test application` **1662 passed**, `nx test desktop` **1148 passed**, `nx test data` **83 passed**; `nx build desktop` green, initial total 1.51 MB / 280.43 kB transfer, no budget warning. `libs/core` and `src-tauri` were not touched, so `nx test core` and `cargo check` do not apply. `npm run quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check` and `git diff --check` were run against the staged tree.
- **Not covered by any check in this repository:** the native re-walk. The regression tests pin both halves at the store seam, which is where the loss becomes observable, but station 3 check `A` item 7 and station 12 are what saw the symptom and they are what should confirm it is gone. The pull request says so rather than implying the suite covers it.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. The new record holds document-library row ids for one browser session, in `sessionStorage`, and nothing leaves the machine. It narrows a destructive path; it does not widen one.
- **Deliberately not done:** `B11`, `B8`, `S1`, `B2` and the print family are untouched - one thing at a time. The orphan draft a regenerate leaves behind when it mints a new row is a pre-existing issue and was not smuggled into this diff. `P1`/`P2` and `P5` remain maintainer decisions.
- **Risks:** a user who restarts the app mid-pass and then cancels keeps two orphan drafts in the Documents library instead of having them cleaned up. That is the chosen failure direction and it is stated in the ADR amendment.
- **Next first action:** `B11` - reproduce the first-attempt cover-letter failure and **capture the provider error on the failed attempt before theorising**. A timeout, a truncated response and a schema rejection need three different fixes, and the retry always working is what keeps this one undiagnosed.

Upgrading the **published** `0.29.2` to `0.29.3` is a better test anyway, because it is the path a real user is on.

### 2026-08-19, the eighth gateway, and two guards that had been narrowing all along

- **Status:** complete. `ProfileSettingsGateway` extracted and **`db.service.ts` deleted**. 461 lines to 0 in eight pull requests. **PR 8 of 8 - the migration is finished.**
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage carried over from the same session's PR 7 (**6/10**), scope unchanged.
- **Branch:** `refactor/profile-settings-gateway`, cut from `origin/main` at `4cb737b0`.
- **Objective:** the last six methods - the profile row, the settings row and the factory reset - and the deletion of the file and its barrel export. Churn re-measured first: **118 files**, of which 24 inject, 87 provide the token in a spec or harness, and 7 only name it in a comment. The recorded "66" counted only files that touch a method; because this pull request deletes the class, every provider had to move.
- **`resetAllData` stays with profile and settings rather than going to `SystemGateway`.** The argument for moving it is real - it wipes every user-data table, not only these two rows, and `SystemGateway` is where the operations belonging to no feature live. The argument that won is the one this migration used three times before: **the consumers decide, not the description.** Its only caller is `SettingsStore`, behind the Settings screen's explicit confirm, and the row it resets to defaults is the settings row. The same principle put the score cache in `JobsGateway` against the written domain list, and `checkArchetypeMatch` there against its banner. Recorded in the gateway's header so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.
- **A sixth provider shape, and it cost two live providers before the suite caught them.** 48 of the 87 specs named none of the six methods in their stub, so their token looked like accumulated migration debt; removing it took out 52 providers. Ten `CvRegenerationStore` tests then failed. The cause: **a class stub whose methods are fields** - `getProfile = jest.fn()`, not `getProfile:` - which the "does this stub name a method?" check missed because it looked for a colon. Two files restored, all three suites green. **Removing a provider is only safe with the suite as the evidence**, and `CODE_QUALITY.md` now lists all six shapes rather than four.
- **Two guards had been enforcing less with every pull request of this migration, and neither would have said so.**
  1. **`cache-signal.guard.spec.ts` reads `*.service.ts`.** It was written when `db.service.ts` was the file it needed to cover; the migration moved every wrapper into `*.gateway.ts`, which that glob does not match. By PR 7 it was checking four files and no gateway at all. It reads both extensions now and asserts it sees **eight** gateways, so a ninth that goes unchecked fails rather than passes.
  2. **`eslint.config.mjs`'s `GATEWAY_INJECTION` listed `DbService` by name.** Deleting the class without touching the rule would have left it **passing on a component that injects `JobsGateway`** - the exact thing ADR-0005 has it forbid, and the worst kind of failure, because the rule's own header cites it as the reason nx's tag check is not sufficient. It matches `[A-Za-z]+Gateway` now. **Verified by mutation, not by reading:** `inject(JobsGateway)` added to `analytics.component.ts` fails `desktop:lint` with the ADR-0005 message and passes again when removed. Recorded as **ADR-0005, amendment sixty-five**.
- **Blind replacement across 118 files rewrote twenty-six comments into lies.** Sentences like "the rest of this stub is still `DbService`'s - those domains have not moved" became statements about `ProfileSettingsGateway` that were both untrue and self-contradictory, and three of them named the wrong gateway outright (`deleteJob` and `upsertApplication` went to `JobsGateway` in PR 7). Each was rewritten by hand. **A repo-wide rename is a mechanical edit to code and a semantic edit to prose**, and the prose has to be read.
- **The gateway spec's trap is that three of the six methods write and one is irreversible.** `upsertProfile` and `updateSettings` each send a `Partial<>` under a key named for the row, and the two call sites look identical. `setProfilePhoto` sends `null` as a **meaningful** value - it removes the photo - so an argument dropped when falsy turns "remove" into "do nothing". And `resetAllData` wipes every user-data table, so the distinct-command test is what stands between it and the other five. Two mutations, both killed: pointing `updateSettings` at `db_upsert_profile` fails 3 tests, and dropping the null photo argument fails 1.
- **Not completed:** nothing in this stream. The gateway migration is finished.
- **Files or packages changed:** `profile-settings.gateway.ts` (65) and `profile-settings.gateway.spec.ts` (110) new; **`db.service.ts` deleted** and its line removed from `libs/data/src/index.ts`; `eslint.config.mjs`; `cache-signal.guard.spec.ts`; 24 source consumers; 87 specs and harnesses, 48 of which also lose a provider they no longer need; 7 comment-only files; `ADR-0005` amendment sixty-five. 124 files total.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check --skip-nx-cache` - clean. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=data,application,desktop --skip-nx-cache` - 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning in `cv-gap-dialog.component.spec.ts`, untouched by this branch. `nx test data --skip-nx-cache` - 9 suites, **83 tests**, green (66 after the deletion removed one parameterised case, then +8 for the new spec and +9 for the widened guard). `nx test application --skip-nx-cache` - 129 suites, **1642 tests**, green. `nx test desktop --skip-nx-cache` - 120 suites, **1148 tests**, green. `nx build desktop` - green. `npm run quality:file-size -- --staged` - **passed**, 0 over budget. `npm run quality:attribution` - passed. `npm run format:check` - passed. `git diff --check` - clean. **Mutations:** 2 on the gateway spec, both killed; 1 on the lint rule, killed.
- **Skipped, honestly:** `cargo check` (nothing under `src-tauri` changed), `check-style-move.mjs` (no stylesheet changed), `nx test core` (`libs/core` unchanged), `nx build web` (the web app imports nothing from `@applye/data`).
- **Privacy/security impact:** none in behaviour - the same six commands with the same arguments reach the same handlers. The **lint** change is a security-adjacent repair rather than a cosmetic one: the rule that keeps data access out of components had stopped covering the classes that now hold it.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** low. Nothing renders differently and the native gate backlog stays at **83**. The screens involved - Settings, Profile, onboarding, and every store reading the settings row - are covered by the manual script's existing stations, so no check was added.

Three pieces of evidence, none of them the banner: it reads **no profile row** - the archetypes arrive as an argument, already parsed by the caller; its **only** caller is `job-intake.service.ts`, which uses it as a zero-token screen on a pasted job description; and its Rust side is `commands::archetypes`, a pure function, not a `db_*` command. A single "make these consistent" edit breaks six commands at once, and the spec asserts the negative directly: those six must not start with `db_`.
  2. **The two sibling setters disagree about their first argument.** `db_set_application_status` sends `id`; `set_application_priority` sends `applicationId`. Both take an application's primary key, both are two-argument setters on the same row, and a copy-paste between them type-checks and sends an argument Rust will not bind.
     Two projections also break their neighbours' naming and are asserted beside them: `listPipelineCards` invokes `db_pipeline_cards`, `getAnalyticsFacts` invokes `db_analytics_facts`.

All three suites passed on the **first** run - against six passes for the previous gateway. The rule earned its place in `CODE_QUALITY.md`.
- **One provider shape the rule still does not name, and it is local to `libs/data`.** `jobs.store.spec.ts` imports `DbService` by **relative path** rather than through `@applye/data`, and puts the provider inline in the `providers:` array on the **same line** - so a pass keyed on the barrel import, or on a provider owning a line of its own, skips it silently. It was found by counting providers against tokens rather than by a test failure, which is the only reason it did not become a fourth failed pass. Recorded as a fifth shape.
- **Twenty of the twenty-four source consumers drop `DbService` entirely.** Four keep both tokens because they still read a profile or a settings value: `tracker-rows.store.ts`, `dashboard.store.ts`, `cv-generate.store.ts` and `job-detail.store.ts`. - **The spec migration failed three times, each on a shape the previous pass had not met.** This is the finding of the watch, and it is now a rule in `CODE_QUALITY.md`:
  1. **A method-name grep** missed specs whose subject injects the gateway without naming any method - `cv-regeneration.store.spec.ts` was the first to fail.

On an `await TestBed...` line that captured the `await`, which was then written onto every hoisted line, producing `await const docsStub = {`. Two files, caught by the suite, repaired. **A regex that assumes indentation is whitespace should assert it.**

All four are asserted rather than sampled, and the mutation confirms it.

### 2026-08-19, the fourth gateway, and the flakiness turns out to have been the machine

- **Status:** complete. `TrackerGateway` extracted; `db.service.ts` **349 to 307/400**. **PR 4 of 8.** The flakiness investigation the previous watch scheduled ran first and **found no repository defect**; the correction is below and it supersedes that watch's next action.

- **Branch:** `refactor/tracker-gateway`, cut from `origin/main` at `bce48076`.

**The flakiness, corrected.** The previous two watches reported the desktop suite as flaky and pointed at a zoneless promise-ordering bug, citing this repository's own recorded lesson. **That reading was wrong, and it was wrong because it was made from test names rather than from error messages.** The actual messages are `Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms for a test` and `for a hook`. **No assertion failed in any of the observed runs.** What was measured:

- the failing run took **133 s**, with its two heaviest suites at **28 s** and **37 s**;
- the same suite on an idle machine, at the default worker count, takes **20 s** and passes twice;
- capped at **two workers** while the machine was loaded, it passes twice, at 79 s and 62 s;
- `tracker.table.spec.ts` alone runs 19 tests in **4 s**, nowhere near the 5 s per-test limit;
- during the failures, `ps` showed Chrome at 74%, WindowServer at 65%, Cursor at 45% and Claude at 44%.

Jest defaults to **nine workers on ten cores** that were already about 70% consumed, so the heaviest component specs did not finish inside the default per-test timeout. **The cause is environmental. No repository change was made**, on the maintainer's decision, and the branch opened for it was deleted unused. Two real but separate observations remain: `cv-detail.cards.spec.ts:90` calls `detectChanges()` on a destroyed fixture (`NG0406`, currently harmless), and jest reports a worker failing to exit gracefully, which points at leaked timers. **Neither causes what was seen.** If it recurs, check the machine's load before the code.

- **The score cache did not travel with the tracker, and the domain list was wrong rather than the boundary.** `scoreCacheGet`, `scoreCacheLatest` and `scoreCacheSave` were described as tracker's when the eight gateways were agreed; their only consumers are `job-scoring.service.ts` and `job-intake.service.ts`, and nothing in the tracker touches them. They go to the jobs gateway. **The description came from me, so this is a correction rather than a discovery.**
- **The seven methods that did move were interleaved through the Jobs section**, not gathered under a banner - the third gateway in a row to find its methods mis-filed.
- **The same spec mistake happened twice in two pull requests, so it is now in `CODE_QUALITY.md`.** `TrackerReportStore` needs only the gateway, but injects `TrackerRowsStore`, which still reads `getSettings` and `deleteJob` through `DbService`; swapping the token wholesale broke three assertions, exactly as `geo-target.store.spec.ts` did during the discover migration. **A spec provides for the subject's dependency graph, not for the subject alone** - and my own previous watch entry said to check this, which is what makes repeating it worth recording.
- **Not completed, and named:** four gateways remain - system, jobs, documents, profile and settings.

### 2026-08-19, the first of eight gateways, and the ratchet refusing on cue

- **Status:** complete. `DraftsGateway` extracted; `db.service.ts` **461 to 426/400**, still over budget and expected to be for six more pull requests. **PR 1 of 8.**
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage **9/10** (radius 2 · ambiguity 2 · risk 1 · verify 2 · unknowns 2), so the grilling gate ran first, in two rounds.

- **Objective:** the maintainer reversed the recorded "not before the ratchet refuses" rule and asked for the cut. The reversal is theirs to make; what was grilled was the **shape**, not the decision.
- **What the grilling settled, and the fact that decided it.** 79 methods, 64 injection sites - and **91 spec files that provide `DbService` by token**, which is the real cost and is invisible from the service. That number is why a single hard-split pull request was rejected: it would have touched about 160 files with a mis-wired method reading as a silent persistence failure. Eight gateways, one pull request each, each a **complete** migration, specs moving with their domain, smallest first.
- **No pull request in this series leaves the dependency pointing the wrong way.** The rejected alternative - create all eight as shims delegating to `DbService`, invert later - would have made `DbService` grow in PR 1 and left the specs asserting against a service production code no longer used.
- **The ratchet refused the first edit, on cue.** `tailoring.service.ts` sat at **exactly 250/250**, so injecting a second dependency put it over. **The line was paid for rather than squeezed:** the pass cache key's string assembly is a function of its arguments and nothing else, so it moved to `tailoring-pass.ts` beside the other pure pass helpers as `passHashInput`. The service goes 250 to **245**, and the thing that moved is I/O-free by construction.
- **The gateway's command strings are the one thing no consumer test can catch.** Every consumer stubs the gateway, so a method invoking `portal_answers_get` where it meant `tailoring_cache_get` leaves all 1642 application tests green and fails only in the running app, where Rust has no command by that name. `drafts.gateway.spec.ts` pins each name and argument shape against a mocked `invoke`, plus a test that counts **distinct** command strings - two methods sharing one passes every per-method assertion. **Verified by mutation:** swapping one string fails two tests, and the count test is the one that catches the collision case. **The strings were equally unverified while they lived on `DbService`**, so this is a seam the move added rather than a gap it opened, and the remaining seven gateways should copy it.
- **`hashText` deliberately did not move.** A dozen callers across profile, documents, dashboard and jobs read it, so it belongs to the system gateway rather than being duplicated into every domain that keys a cache on it. All three migrated services therefore inject **both** `DraftsGateway` and `DbService`, and each says at the injection site why.
