### 2026-08-19, the native gate gets a route, and the file-size stream ends

- **Status:** complete. `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_SCRIPT.md` written: the backlog's **81 checks across fifteen sections** ordered into **fifteen stations**, numbered 0 to 14, one sitting. This is the last deliverable of the file-size stream, and the point at which the work stops being an agent's.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage **5/10** (radius 0 · ambiguity 1 · risk 1 · verify 1 · unknowns 2), unknowns 2 because the database rows each section needs are in `tools/capture/seed.mjs`, not in the backlog.
- **Branch:** `docs/native-gate-script`, cut from `origin/main` at `48a3b4ec`.
- **Objective:** the previous watch's next first action, and the thing every watch since 2026-08-14 has deferred.
- **The ordering is the deliverable, not the list.** Three constraints decide it and are written down as the design rather than left to be inferred: **the welcome screen needs a database that has never been written to**, so C4 is walked before anything is seeded and each of its three launches needs its own fresh profile; everything else needs real rows, so one seed run carries the pass; and the destructive and paid checks are held to the end.
- **What the seed cannot produce is produced by an earlier station.** `seed.mjs` writes the profile, eight jobs, applications, stages, history and a Discover source - and no documents. So station 3 creates the CV that stations 4, 5 and 6 all use, station 7 archives the tracker row it then needs, and station 8 makes a card overdue before opening the composer. That chain is why the stations are in the order they are rather than in backlog order.
- **C4 needed splitting into three launches rather than one.** "Both ways out work" consumes the fresh state, and the short-window check has to be set up **before** launch, so one profile cannot serve all five of its checks. Reading the section as a single sitting would have burned the state on the first exit.
- **Every check has exactly one station, and the file proves it.** A coverage table at the foot maps all fifteen sections to their stations, splitting the three that straddle one (A across 3/12/13, C across 4/5/6, C9 across 10/13, D across 11/12). Counted programmatically against the backlog: **81 in, 81 placed**.
- **The two files keep different jobs, stated at the top of each.** The backlog is where a check is ticked; the watch log is where a failure is recorded; the script holds no state. The backlog now points at the script as its route.
- **Not completed, and it is not completable here:** the walk itself. Every check in it exists precisely because synthetic clicks do not reach the Tauri webview and every `invoke` rejects outside it.
- **Files or packages changed:** `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_SCRIPT.md` new (292 lines); `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md` gains a pointer to it; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** documentation only, so the code gates do not apply and are **not** claimed. `npm run format:check` - clean. `npm run quality:file-size` - reports **"no changed source files to check"**, which is what it says on a documentation-only diff and is not a pass; `--all` is unchanged at one file over budget. `npm run quality:attribution` - passed. `git diff --check` - clean. Coverage counted programmatically from the backlog's checkboxes: 81 checks, 15 sections, each mapped once. **Not run and not applicable:** every `nx` target, `cargo check`, `check-style-move` - no source file changed.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. The script names a database path and a seed command the repository already documents; the seed writes invented companies and `example.com` addresses only.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** the release check (E) is a separate station rather than part of the sitting, because it needs an installed `0.29.1` rather than a dev build. The paid checks are a station of their own with an explicit "skipping is a legitimate outcome, say so in the watch entry" - the alternative was leaving them looking done. Roughly ninety minutes is an estimate, not a measurement.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none to the application. The risk is that the script goes stale: it is ordered around what `seed.mjs` produces today, so a change to the seed changes the setup half of several stations.
- **Open issues or blockers:** the walk itself, which is the maintainer's. `db.service.ts` 461/400 remains the one file over budget, by decision.
- **Next first action:** **walk it.** Start at station 0 with the backup command, because station 0 deletes the profile. Record failures in this file, tick `NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md`, and delete a ticked item once driven - a ticked item left there reads as outstanding on the next read.
- **Evidence:** the programmatic count of the backlog's checkboxes per section; `seed.mjs` and `seed-jobs.mjs` for what the seed actually writes; `first-launch.component.ts` for the `healthCheckSeen` gate that forces C4 to the front; `db.rs` for the app-data path the backup and fresh-profile commands use.

- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage **4/10** (radius 1 · ambiguity 1 · risk 1 · verify 1 · unknowns 0).
- **Branch:** `fix/cv-save-template-modal-buttons`, cut from `origin/main` at `3e22d75a`.
- **Objective:** the bug the previous watches filed and did not fix, authorised by the maintainer.
- **The bug was in a comment as much as in the markup.** The stylesheet opened by stating `.btn-ghost` and `.btn-primary` are "global, from `libs/ui`". `libs/ui/src/styles/_button.scss` declares the `.btn--ghost` BEM family instead. Compiling `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss` and reading the output settles it: the only match anywhere in the built global sheet is `.profile .btn-ghost`, nested where this dialog can never satisfy it, and **`.btn-primary` has no global declaration at all**.
- **It predates the component split**, which is worth stating because the split is the obvious suspect. `git log -S` over `cv-detail/` shows the class strings arrive with the original feature commit `56852c59` and the page's own stylesheet never declared them; #465 only moved the markup.
- **The two existing tests were selecting by the broken names, and that is why nothing caught it.** `cv-detail.cards.spec.ts` clicked `.btn-ghost` and read `.btn-primary`'s `disabled`. Both passed, because the classes were in the DOM - they simply matched no CSS. **A class name that matches nothing fails silently**, so a test that uses one as a selector is coverage of the name and not of the styling. Retargeting them was part of the fix, not incidental to it.
- **The regression test asserts the property, not the change.** `.btn` plus the right variant per button, **counted in both directions** so the two are not interchangeable, and the **absence of the dead hyphenated names** - without that half, re-adding `class="btn-primary"` beside the directive would pass. Verified to fail before the fix and pass after: 3 new failures on the unfixed tree, 5 assertions green on the fixed one, plus the 2 retargeted.
- **The fix is `ButtonDirective` rather than a rule in the sheet**, as the file itself now records: the directive is the one place those class names are written, so the dialog cannot drift from the design system again by copying a name.
- **Not completed, and named:** the manual gate script, which is the last item in this stream.
- **Files or packages changed:** `cv-save-template-modal.component.{html,ts,scss}`; `cv-save-template-modal.component.spec.ts` new; `cv-detail.cards.spec.ts` two selectors retargeted; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check` - clean. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` - clean, and **the pre-existing warning is gone**, because it lived in a file this watch did not touch and the tree it was measured against has moved. `nx test desktop --skip-nx-cache` - 120 suites, **1148 tests**, all passing (5 new). Failing-first run on the unfixed tree - 3 failed, exactly the new styling assertions. `nx build desktop` - succeeded, initial total 1.50 MB / 279.97 kB, no budget error. `check-style-move.mjs --base origin/main` on the dialog's sheet - **lossless** (only a comment changed). `quality:file-size`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` - clean. **Not run and not applicable:** `nx test core`/`application` (no library changed), `cargo check`, `nx build web`.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. Presentation only; the dialog's outputs and disabled logic are unchanged and asserted to be.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** the directive's default `size="md"` is used rather than the onboarding screens' `lg`, because this is a dialog action row and every other dialog in the app uses the default.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** low. The buttons gain the design system's padding, height and colours, so the dialog's action row is taller than the broken version was - which is the intended appearance, not a regression. `NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md` gains section **C11** with one check: the paint itself, which no test can assert. The backlog goes 80 to **81**.
- **Open issues or blockers:** none new. The Tauri manual gate is the maintainer's to drive.
- **Next first action:** **write the manual gate script** - turn `NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md`'s 81 checks across sixteen sections into one walkable pass: the database rows each section needs, the screens in the order that lets one setup serve several checks, what to look at, and which checks wipe data so they go last (C9's clear-feed is one). This is the deliverable that ends the stream; the maintainer drives it and this session cannot.
- **Evidence:** the compiled global sheet, which contains `.profile .btn-ghost` and no `.btn-primary` at all; `git log -S` over `cv-detail/`; the failing-first run; the stashed-fix run confirming the retargeted selectors also fail without it.

### 2026-08-18, the document model splits six ways, and the reconnaissance behind it was half wrong

- **Status:** complete. `document.model.ts` **504 into six files** of 24 to 142 lines. The repository goes to **1** file over budget - `db.service.ts` 461/400, which stays by decision - down from 18 across fifteen watches.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5 (verdict said Sonnet; the session model cannot be switched from inside it, stated once and continued). No subagents. Triage **6/10** (radius 2 · ambiguity 0 · risk 1 · verify 2 · unknowns 1).
- **Branch:** `refactor/document-model-split`, cut from `origin/main` at `6dbaa1d6`.
- **Objective:** the second of the two pull requests the grilling round ordered, after #480 merged.
- **The split follows the seams already in the file**, chosen by symbol rather than by line: CV content, cover-letter content, page settings, CV style, the document library (which is the only file that knows both content kinds exist, because `DocumentContent` is their union), and the import/parsed shapes. Symbols were cut with their doc comments by parsing top-level `export`s, not by slicing line ranges - the mistake that produced broken blocks two watches ago.
- **The property a public-API split has to prove is that the surface did not move, and it is checked rather than asserted.** Walking `libs/core/src/index.ts` and every `export *` under it gives **315 exported symbols before and 315 after**, nothing lost, nothing newly exported. A word-multiset audit of the six files against the original shows every identifier, literal and doc word survives.
- **The reconnaissance was half wrong, and it is worth naming.** The grilling round recorded "nothing imports the path deeply; one internal importer, `cv-theme.model.ts`" - because the grep behind it excluded `libs/core/src`. There are **fourteen** deep importers, all inside `libs/core`. The claim was true about everything outside the library, which is what mattered for the decision, but it was stated more broadly than the evidence supported.
- **A missing type import degrades a type instead of failing where it is missing.** `CvSectionKey` was unresolved in the new `cv-style.model.ts`, so `Partial<Record<CvSectionKey, CvSectionStyle>>` collapsed into a plain index signature, and the visible failure was a wave of `TS4111: comes from an index signature` in **two other spec files**, twenty lines from anything I had touched. Chasing the symptom would have edited the specs; the fix was one import.
- **`nx run desktop:type-check` reported none of it.** It compiled clean while `libs/core` did not, which is the second time this watch that a green check covered nothing: `nx test core` found all four missing imports. **The desktop type-check is not a check on `libs/core`.**
- **Not completed, and named:** the `cv-save-template-modal` unstyled-button bug and the manual gate script.
- **Files or packages changed:** `document.model.ts` deleted into `cv-content.model.ts`, `cover-letter-content.model.ts`, `page-settings.model.ts`, `cv-style.model.ts`, `document-library.model.ts` and `cv-import.model.ts`; `libs/core/src/index.ts`; fourteen deep importers inside `libs/core`; `document.model.spec.ts` renamed `document-models.spec.ts`; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check` - clean (and see above for what that does not cover). `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop,core --skip-nx-cache` - 0 errors; core's 17 warnings are **pre-existing and unchanged in count**, confirmed against a stashed tree. `nx test core --skip-nx-cache` - **29 suites, 466 tests**, all passing. `nx test desktop --skip-nx-cache` - 119 suites, **1143 tests**. `nx test application --skip-nx-cache` - 129 suites, **1642 tests**. `nx build desktop` - succeeded, initial total 1.50 MB / **279.99 kB**, 0.17 kB below the previous watch, no budget error. `nx build web` - succeeded; initial 504.25 kB against a 500 kB budget, the **pre-existing** 4.25 kB overage recorded in this file and unchanged. Public-surface diff - 315/315. Word-multiset content audit - nothing lost. `quality:file-size`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` - clean. **Not run and not applicable:** `cargo check` (nothing under `src-tauri`), `check-style-move` (no stylesheet changed).
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. Type declarations only; no runtime behaviour, no data path.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** `CoverLetterStyle` sits with the cover-letter content rather than with page settings, because it is that document's style. `LibraryDocType`, `DocumentSource` and `DocumentContent` sit with the library rather than with either content kind. The old path is gone rather than kept as a barrel: the deep importers are all inside `libs/core` and were updated, and a barrel existing only for a path nobody outside uses would be two places to add a type.

### 2026-08-18, the CV preview's six atoms leave the page, and a mutation finds what the suite could not

- **Status:** complete. `cv-preview.component.html` **779 to 126/300** - the largest file in the repository, now the sheet, the overflow warning and one `<h3>`. The class 389 to **309/400**. The repository goes to **2** files over budget, and **no stylesheet and no template is over budget any more.**
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage **8/10** (radius 2 · ambiguity 0 · risk 2 · verify 2 · unknowns 2), ambiguity 0 because the grilling round settled the shape first.
- **Branch:** `refactor/cv-preview-sections`, cut from `origin/main` at `f1398e22`.
- **Objective:** the first of the three gated files, after the maintainer's `aif-grilling` round chose per-section children over a leaf component.
- **The grilling changed the plan twice, and the second time on a fact I only had after reading both blocks.** Round two agreed summary and bullet would share one child because they share the word-token protocol. They do not: summary is `div > p|textarea` committing through `commitSummary`, bullet is `ul > li|textarea` committing through `commitExperienceBullet`, and what they share is a 15-line loop calling a different toggle in each. Merging them meant a mode flag on one component serving two call sites - the shape that has leaked twice here. Round three took six children, one per atom, with `#sectionTitleTpl` staying because a component for one `<h3>` is all boilerplate. **That is also the plan the file itself recorded**, in the header comment left by the header extraction.
- **The seam is not the repetition.** The handoff named the 17 near-identical `@if (isEditingLeaf(...))` pairs as the real seam; there are **15**, and they are not the boundary - a component for them would put 15 new host elements into the printed inline flow the measurement pass paginates on.
- **The check that mattered is not the test suite, and the suite proved it.** Angular stamps markup with the DECLARING component's attribute, so a rule left behind stops matching markup that moved, and `quality:style-move` cannot see it because no declaration was lost. So: a reachability audit, per child, asserting that every `cvpreview__*` class it renders is reachable from its own compiled sheet. **It was validated against a known answer before its clean result was believed** - deleting one `@use` from the languages child makes it flag `section-start` and `section-title`. Four new partials carry what more than one atom needs: `_cv-preview-section` (4 consumers), `_cv-preview-word` (2), `_cv-preview-entry` (2) and `_cv-preview-inline-editor` (4).
- **Two selectors were dead and are deleted:** `.cvpreview__skill-row--editor` and `.cvpreview__languages--editor`, declared in the sheet and rendered by nothing in `apps/` or `libs/`, with no dynamic class construction anywhere. `check-style-move` reports exactly those two and nothing else.
- **A mutation survived, and it was a real gap.** Pointing the education entry's click and Enter handlers at the section title instead of the entry left all 1139 tests green. **The first run mis-attributed the kill**: two failures appeared while two mutations were live, and both belonged to the other one - re-running the education mutation alone is what showed it surviving. Experience was covered leaf by leaf and education was covered nowhere, which only became visible once the atom was its own component. `cv-preview.education.spec.ts` adds four assertions, counted per call site in both directions, and they kill it.
- **The word-bold rewrite moved to `CvPreviewEditingService`**, which owns the emit sink a child cannot reach - the same "rewrite a section and publish it" shape as every commit beside it. The styling spec now reaches it through the component's own injector, which asserts the same wiring end to end.
- **Not completed, and named:** `document.model.ts` ships as a second pull request, per the round-two decision. `db.service.ts` stays by decision. The `cv-save-template-modal` bug and the manual gate script are untouched.
- **Files or packages changed:** `cv-preview.component.{html,ts,scss}`; six child components (18 files); four new partials; `cv-preview-editing.service.ts` +25; `cv-preview.styling.spec.ts` retargeted; `cv-preview.education.spec.ts` new; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check` - clean. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` - 0 errors, 1 warning, **pre-existing** (confirmed by re-running against a stashed tree). The pre-commit lesson repeated itself: eight orphaned imports survived the type-check and only lint caught them. `nx test desktop --skip-nx-cache` - **119 suites, 1143 tests, all passing** (4 new). `nx build desktop` - succeeded, initial total 1.50 MB / 280.16 kB, no budget error. Reachability audit across all eight preview components - clean, and validated against a known-bad state first. `check-style-move.mjs --base origin/main` across all thirteen sheets - **exactly the two deleted dead selectors**. Word-multiset payload audit of the template before/after - the only losses are the deliberate `selectable(renderMode)` to `selectable()` rewrite and the two renamed toggles. `quality:file-size --staged`, `quality:attribution`, `format:check`, `git diff --check` - clean. **Not run and not applicable:** `nx test application` (no library changed), `cargo check` (nothing under `src-tauri`), `nx build web` (untouched).
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. No data path, no persistence and no new I/O; the children render what the page already had.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** six children rather than five or seven, per the grilling round. `#sectionTitleTpl` stays on the page. `.cvpreview__entry-meta` rides along in the shared entry partial and is emitted by the education child, which cannot match it - one declaration of the pair was judged better than two that drift. `showIndustry` is resolved by the parent and passed as a boolean so the child needs no theme knowledge.

### 2026-08-18, the editor shell splits, and the proof is a byte-for-byte diff

- **Status:** complete. `_editor-shell.scss` **460 to 26/400**, as a barrel over ten partials. The repository goes 4 to **3** files over budget, and **no stylesheet is over budget any more.** All three remaining items are blocked on the maintainer's decision rather than on work.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. Triage **7/10** (radius 2 · ambiguity 1 · risk 1 · verify 2 · unknowns 1).
- **Branch:** `refactor/editor-shell-partials`, cut from `origin/main` at `f1398e22`.
- **Objective:** the previous watch's next first action - the last unblocked file, and the only one in this series that is a global partial rather than a component-scoped sheet.
- **The risk here is different from every other file in the stream, and it drove the verification rather than the design.** This partial is `@use`d exactly once, from `apps/desktop/src/styles.scss`, and emitted **unwrapped into the global sheet**; eleven templates across both document editors render `docedit-*` classes without declaring them. So a mistake shows on pages the diff never mentions. **The split is by responsibility and by nothing else:** ten partials under `editor-shell/` - card, disclosure, chips, meta, style-grid, color-row, margin-grid, note, reset, section - cut on the section banners the file already carried, largest 102 lines.
- **`styles.scss` was compiled with `sass` before and after and the two outputs diffed: 2432 lines, identical.** That is the check this file needed, and it is stronger than the one the protocol names. `check-style-move` across the barrel and all ten children was run anyway and reports lossless - it compares declarations per selector, so it would not have caught a reordering that changed which rule wins, and the byte diff does.
- **`@use` order is emission order, so the barrel's list is the cascade**, and the barrel now says so. Nothing in the file relies on that today - the one cross-partial pair, `.docedit-style-section .docedit-color-row` in `_style-grid.scss` against `.docedit-color-row` in `_color-row.scss`, is decided by specificity, two classes against one, and would win from either position. **That is a fact about today's rules, not a property of the arrangement:** the next same-specificity rule added to a partial is decided by where its partial sits in the list, which is why the order is written down rather than left to be inferred.
- **The header comment was wrong, and it is the one thing deliberately not preserved.** It said both `cv-detail.component.scss` and `cover-letter-detail.component.scss` `@use` this partial and that view encapsulation scopes the output per component. **Neither does**, and has not since the hoist: both sheets open with a comment saying the styles arrive globally. A comment describing the opposite of the file's reach is worse than none, because it is what a session reads before deciding whether a rule is safe to move - it would have said "scoped, safe" about a global sheet.
- **No manual check is owed for this one, and that is a claim rather than an omission.** `NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md` gains nothing: the emitted CSS is byte-identical, so there is no rendered difference for a manual walk to find. The backlog stays at **73** unticked checks across fourteen sections.
- **Not completed, and named:** nothing else was attempted. The three gated files, the `cv-save-template-modal` unstyled-button bug and the manual gate script are all untouched.
- **Files or packages changed:** `_editor-shell.scss` rewritten as a barrel; `editor-shell/` ten new partials; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, this file.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check` - clean. `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop --skip-nx-cache` - clean. `nx test desktop` - **1139 tests, all passing**, unchanged count (no behaviour changed, so no test was added; the emitted-CSS diff is the assertion). `nx build desktop` - succeeded, initial total 1.50 MB / 280.19 kB, no budget error; the one sass deprecation warning is **pre-existing** and points at `cover-letter-list.component.scss`'s `@import`. `check-style-move.mjs --base origin/main` across all eleven sheets - **lossless**. `sass` compile of `styles.scss` before and after - **identical, 2432 lines**. `quality:file-size --staged` - passed; `--all` reports 0/149 stylesheets over budget. `quality:attribution`, `prettier --check`, `git diff --check` - clean. **Not run and not applicable:** `nx test application` (no library changed), `cargo check` (nothing under `src-tauri`), `nx build web` (untouched).
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. No TypeScript, no template and no behaviour changed.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** the barrel keeps the name `_editor-shell.scss` rather than becoming `editor-shell/_index.scss`, because thirteen comments across the repository name this file and an index would leave every one of them pointing at a path that no longer exists. Sass resolves `@use './app/pages/documents/editor-shell'` to `_editor-shell.scss` with no ambiguity while `editor-shell/_index.scss` does not exist, which the build confirms.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none measurable. The global sheet is byte-identical, which is the whole of the risk surface for this file.
- **Open issues or blockers:** the three gated files need one `aif-grilling` round, not three. The `cv-save-template-modal` unstyled-button bug is still open and authorised. The Tauri manual gate is the maintainer's to drive.
- **Next first action:** **bring all three gated questions in one `aif-grilling` round** - `cv-preview.component.html` 779/300 (seventeen near-identical `@if (isEditingLeaf(...))` pairs, one inline-editing protocol repeated per field, not nine independent atoms), `document.model.ts` 504/400 (splitting it changes a `libs/core` public API) and `db.service.ts` 461/400 (**including whether its recorded "not before the ratchet refuses the next method" rule still stands**, rather than assuming "do all the files" overrides it). Ask; do not choose.
- **Evidence:** the `sass` before/after diff of `styles.scss`; `check-style-move`'s lossless report across eleven sheets; the removed-line multiset audit, whose only unmatched lines are the six of the corrected header comment; `grep -rn "editor-shell"` across `apps/` and `libs/`, which finds exactly one `@use`, in `styles.scss`.

- **The old verdict was right about extraction and wrong about the file.** What remains genuinely is the page's own chrome - each block is roughly ten lines of markup, and a component per block would be worse than leaving it. **But a reachability audit had never been run on this page**, and the file held 48 lines that were dead or declared in the wrong place. That is only findable by measuring; re-reading the conclusion would have reproduced it.
- **The audit tool was validated against a known answer before its result was believed**, as the protocol demands: run against `cv-detail.component.scss` at `f79c9b1e~1` it flags exactly the `.cvdetail__*` families #464 deleted. Its documented false positive then fired exactly as expected - the five `.dv-console__line--*` modifiers read as unreachable and are applied through `[class]="'dv-console__line--' + line.tone"`. **A negative result from that tool is only worth what the validation run is worth.**
- **Two selectors are genuinely dead:** `.dv-footer__actions` and `.dv-footer__confirm` appear in no template, no TypeScript and no dynamic binding **anywhere in the repository**, checked by grep across `apps/` and `libs/` rather than in the page alone.
- **Four of the six keyframes were declared on the page and belonged elsewhere, and two of them the page never used at all.** `dv-pulse`'s only consumer is `_discover-controls.scss`; `dv-slidein`'s is the sources drawer. **Neither declares a copy**, so the page was emitting them on behalf of files that would have gone silently unanimated the moment its rules were deleted. **This is the exact mirror of the tracker's `jtIn`/`jtPop` case**, where every consumer _had_ an identical copy and deletion was safe - the same shape of finding with the opposite answer, which is why the check has to be "who declares it" rather than "who uses it". `dv-pulse`, `dv-shimmer` and `dv-fade` moved into the global partial `styles.scss` already emits once; `dv-slidein` moved into the drawer.
- **The clear-feed confirmation became a component at no cost in duplicated rules**, because `.dv-btn` and its modifiers already come from that same global partial. **The overlay stays on the page**: a click outside is the page's own cancel, and keeping the two apart is what lets the dialog stop a click on itself from reaching it.
- **The dialog had never been opened by a test**, and it is the one destructive action on this page. Eight assertions were written against it before the extraction.
- **Two mutations survived the first pass and both were about the same blind spot.** A cancel wired to the destructive handler passed, because the assertion did not drain the macrotask a wipe needs - **"nothing happened" has to be asserted in the state where it would have happened.** And the backdrop had no test at all, so pointing it at the wipe changed nothing; it is a separate handler on a much larger target next to a destructive action. **The second attempt at the first mutation also hit the wrong element** - `cancelClearFeed` appears twice and the rewrite took the backdrop rather than the button, which is the "first of N identical strings" trap for the second time this session. Both gaps are covered now.
- **Not completed, and named:** nothing else was attempted.
- **Files or packages changed:** `discover.component.{ts,html,scss}`, `_discover-controls.scss`, `discover-sources-drawer.component.scss`; `discover-clear-confirm/` (three files) new; `discover.clear-confirm.spec.ts` new; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/product/CURRENT_STATE.md`, `docs/internal/NATIVE_GATE_BACKLOG.md`, this file.

- **What did not move is the finding, not what did.** `.card` itself **stays on the page**, written onto the child's own host element. Three rules in `_drag.scss` depend on it being a page-declared class: `.card.cdk-drag-preview` has to match the clone the CDK appends **outside every component view**, `.card.cdk-drag-animating` has to beat it at equal specificity by coming later in the same file, and `.col__list.cdk-drop-list-dragging .card` reaches from the drop list into the card. `drag-styles.spec.ts` compiles the page sheet and asserts precisely that cascade - moving `.card` would have moved the thing that test is about.
- **`cdkDrag` stays on the host for a second reason, and this one fails silently.** `CdkDropList` finds its draggables through **content children**, so a `cdkDrag` inside the child's own view would not be content of the list. Drag-and-drop would have stopped working with type-check, lint, the whole suite and the build all green. The host-element form keeps the draggable a direct child of the list, which is why the child renders the card's insides rather than the card.
- **An `<ng-content>` was written and then deleted, because deleting it changed nothing.** The drag placeholder is declared between the component's tags and looks like projected content, but `*cdkDragPlaceholder` is a structural directive that renders nothing at its declaration site: `CdkDrag` finds it as a content child, keeps the `TemplateRef`, and instantiates it itself when a drag starts. Projection was never involved. **Mutation is what said so - a line no mutation can break is inert rather than covered**, and that is a reason to delete it rather than to write a test for it.
- **The page had no DOM spec at all**, only `drag-styles.spec.ts`, which compiles the stylesheet and never renders anything. Eighteen assertions were written and passed against the unsplit board first, with the interview stage track **counted per column**: five columns draw the same card markup, an application keeps its stage data after moving on to Offer, and "a track exists somewhere on the board" passes while every column has grown one.
- **Two mutations survived the first pass; one was a real gap and one was inert.** The gap: a column badge counting what the column holds rather than what the search leaves visible was invisible until the filter test asserted the badge as well - **a count and the thing it counts have to be asserted in the same state.** The inert one was the `<ng-content>` above. **The wiring a DOM query cannot see is asserted through the CDK's own directives instead**: each card is a `CdkDrag` on an `app-pipeline-card` host carrying `.card`, with a resolved placeholder template and a `dropContainer` that is a real `CdkDropList`. `_draggables` was tried first and is not public in this CDK version; `dropContainer` is.

It caught nothing, which is the outcome a safety net should usually have - but it was in place before anything moved.
- **The seam was repetition, not sections.** Six cards - funnel, score distribution, score vs outcome, time to response, pipeline aging, locations - each wrote out the same fifteen lines of bar markup. **They differ only in their data**, and the page's computeds had already resolved every difference into a value, so `AnalyticsBarListComponent` is a view over one row shape (`name`, `valueText`, `widthPct`, optional `fill` / `nameColor` / `convText` / `convOf`) and every predicate that distinguishes the six stays in the page. Two more came out for size rather than repetition: `AnalyticsKpiRowComponent` and `AnalyticsTrendComponent`.
- **Three findings worth carrying.**
  - **The KPI row renders its own loading placeholders, and that is a fact rather than a mode.** The store returns no view until the facts load, so `tiles()` is already empty exactly while the page is loading. The alternatives were both worse: a second copy of the tile markup in the page's skeleton branch would have made `.ana-tile` shared vocabulary for no reason, and a boolean `skeleton` input would have been the hidden mode `CODE_QUALITY.md` warns about, saying the same thing twice.

  - **Projection removed work that looked like it needed inputs.** The per-card notes and the funnel's leakage bar are the page's own sentences. Passed through `<ng-content>` they stay in the page's view, so `.ana-note` and `.ana-leak` keep the page's rules and never had to move or be duplicated.

With one component serving six call sites, the property is that the column belongs to the funnel and to nothing else - which has to be counted **per list**, not in total. The second was the trend's follow-ups polyline: "a polyline exists" cannot see it disappear, because the applications line is always drawn. Both now fail, along with a third mutation collapsing the two halves of the conversion column into one flag (score vs outcome renders the caption without the percentage). **Seven mutations, all killed.**

Angular scopes a component's compiled CSS to its own view, so that is exactly the reachability condition - and content projected into a child still carries the parent's attribute, so it is covered for free by reading the page template. Only the rightmost compound is required to match, which is the conservative direction: an unreachable ancestor was reported as a separate tier and neither sheet had one.

The collision question never arose: **321 of the 640 lines could not reach a single element.** Angular scopes a component's compiled CSS to its own view, so a `.cvdetail__*` rule declared on the page never matched markup a section editor declares - and the page's sheet defined 53 `cvdetail__` classes while the page's own template rendered 24.

- **`quality:style-move` was then run in a shape worth reusing:** the page's sheet plus **all five section editors** in one invocation. Because the tool takes the union across the files listed, the 23 duplicated groups are covered by the children's identical copies and are not reported, while the genuinely dead family is. It printed **11 lost, 0 gained, all of them `cvdetail__style-*`** - which is the mechanical version of the argument above rather than a second opinion on it.
- **A partial would have been wrong twice.** It would have given three component bundles a global copy of rules only one of them needs, and it would have preserved as shared vocabulary something that was already dead. `styles.scss` is untouched; nothing new is global.

### 2026-08-14, an architecture review that found the dead scaffolding and three lying documents

- **Status:** complete.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No subagents. No `aif-grilling` round: the maintainer approved the scope explicitly after the review, and nothing here changes a `libs/` public API in a way with two readings - the one public-API change, dropping `Ui` from `libs/ui`'s index, removes a symbol with zero consumers.

- **Commits:** `3aa02f65`.
- **Pull request:** [#446](https://github.com/vitala89/applye/pull/446).
- **Objective:** answer where Applye sits on the monolith → modular-monolith → monorepo → multi-monorepo → microfrontend progression, check the Tauri 2 + Angular setup against current practice, and remove whatever the review proved dead.
- **Completed:**
  - **The architecture question is answered, and the answer is "stage three, and deliberately not stage four or five."** One Nx monorepo, `apps/{desktop,web,mobile}` + six `libs/`, five `@applye/*` aliases, and boundaries enforced by `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` rather than by convention - which is stricter than the modular-monolith stage it is compared against, where module isolation is an agreement. **Microfrontends are ruled out on a technical ground, not a taste one:** `tauri.conf.json` sets `script-src 'self'`, so a Module Federation remote entry cannot load without weakening the CSP of an application that holds API keys in the OS keychain and the user's database on disk; the app is local-first and must work offline; and there is no independent deploy target for a fragment, because a release is a signed installer plus `latest.json`. The role "ship part of the app without rebuilding the shell" is already played by the updater. The 17 `loadComponent` routes already provide the part of the microfrontend benefit that applies here.
  - **Thirteen dead files removed** - the `lib-ui`, `lib-data` and `lib-i18n` generator scaffolds and the zero-byte `apps/desktop/src/app/app.scss`. Found by hashing every `.ts`, `.html` and `.scss` in `apps` and `libs`: the three scaffold stylesheets and `app.scss` are byte-identical, which is what a four-way duplicate is for. `libs/ui/src/index.ts` was exporting `Ui`, so this is a public-API narrowing with no consumers.
  - **`dialog:allow-open` dropped from `capabilities/default.json`**, because the plugin's `permissions/default.toml` defines `dialog:default` as `["allow-message", "allow-save", "allow-open"]`. `opener` was deliberately **not** collapsed to its default set: naming `allow-open-url` and `allow-default-urls` by hand is what keeps `allow-reveal-item-in-dir` out, and that is the tighter grant.
  - **Three governance documents corrected.** `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/governance/CODE_QUALITY.md` all still described `COMPONENTS_STILL_USING_THE_GATEWAY` as live - at "a list of 1" in two of them and at 26 in the third - and `CODE_QUALITY.md` also claimed `type:data` was still in `type:app`'s allowlist. Both statements were deleted from `eslint.config.mjs` by amendments fifty-five and fifty-six. The error ran in the permissive direction: an agent following the docs would go looking for an escape hatch that no longer exists.
- **Not completed:** nothing in the approved scope. Three findings from the same review were **recorded rather than acted on**, because each is a separate change: `jobs.component.ts` at 977/400 is the one real architectural debt left; ten Rust `commands/*.rs` modules run 598-851 lines and mix IPC handler with domain logic, which is the same disease the frontend already cured; and `libs/skills` has no `project.json` while `ai/skills.rs` reads its `.md` files through `include_str!`, so a prompt edit is invisible to the nx graph and its cache.
- **Files or packages changed:** 13 deletions across `libs/ui`, `libs/data`, `libs/i18n`, `apps/desktop`; `libs/ui/src/index.ts`; `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`; `CLAUDE.md`; `AGENTS.md`; `docs/governance/CODE_QUALITY.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`; this file.

### 2026-08-13, level three: the header becomes a component, and its styles do not follow it

- **Status:** complete. Every automated gate observed passing, and the rendered check both **caught a regression** and confirmed the fix.
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code, Opus 5. No new grilling - the shape was settled in this session's earlier rounds. No subagents.
- **Branch:** `refactor/cv-preview-header-component`
- **Commits:** one code commit, one documentation commit
- **Pull request:** pending at time of writing
- **Objective:** The header pilot - `#headerTpl` out of `cv-preview.component.html` into a child component.
- **Completed:** `cv-preview-header/` (component, template, stylesheet). `cv-preview.component.html` **895 -> 779/300**; `cv-preview.component.scss` **392 -> 211**; the class **355 -> 350** as the first two delegators died. `_cv-preview-atom.scss` added for rules every atom shares. ADR-0005 amendment sixty-three, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`.
- **Not completed:** The other seven blocks. Granularity for the sweep is still open and should be decided against this pilot's evidence rather than in advance.
- **Files or packages changed:** `apps/desktop/src/app/pages/documents/cv-detail/cv-preview/` only, plus documentation.
- **Validation:** `nx run-many --target=type-check` (7), `nx run-many --target=lint --skip-nx-cache` (7, 0 errors), `nx run-many --target=test --skip-nx-cache` (7; 966 desktop tests, count unchanged - the existing preview specs render the header through the child), `nx build desktop`, `npm run quality:file-size`, `npm run quality:attribution`, `npm run quality:style-move --base main`, `npm run format:check`, `git diff --check`. All observed. **Rendered check on a real two-page CV, twice**: it failed the first time and passed after the fix.
- **The regression, and why it matters more than the extraction:** the first rendered check showed the name as `Mira Halvorsen` where the design says `MIRA HALVORSEN`. Angular's emulated encapsulation binds a rule to the component that DECLARES the markup, so moving the header's markup into a child stopped every `.cvpreview__*` rule in the parent stylesheet from matching it - uppercase, letter-spacing, the photo float, the selection ring and the chip, all gone. **Every gate stayed green**, including `quality:style-move`, which reported "0 selectors lost declarations" and was right: nothing had been deleted, the rules had stopped applying. **A gate that compares stylesheet contents cannot see a selector that still exists and no longer matches.** Fifth regression in this campaign reachable only from a screen.
- **Privacy/security impact:** None. Presentation only.
- **Decisions and assumptions:** (1) **The declaration injector was verified, not assumed** - the child injects all four services and the evidence is that no spec threw `NullInjectorError`. (2) **Six inputs, all data**, against the ~20 the 2026-08-04 decision measured; that decision was right about its file and was discharged by #439 and #440. (3) **Rules split by ownership**: per-atom rules move with their atom, shared ones go to `_cv-preview-atom.scss` and are `@use`d by both, each copy carrying its own component's attribute - the duplication is the mechanism, not a cost. (4) `selectable()` is bound once on the child rather than at 30 call sites, for the same 100-column reason that shaped this whole family. (5) `@if (section().title; as title)` is required, not stylistic: the template type-checker cannot narrow across a signal call.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** **One limit is now recorded in the partial**, because the next seven blocks will meet it: `.cvpreview__selected:has(.cvpreview__element-selected)` needs the container and its leaves to share an encapsulation attribute, so an atom may not be split across two components. It would fail silently, on a screen only.
- **Open issues or blockers:** The `quality:style-move` blind spot is real and now documented, but nothing was done about it - a gate that could catch this would have to compare RENDERED styles, which is a different kind of check.
- **Next first action:** The second block, with the pattern proven. `#eduEntryTpl` (161) or `#skillsTpl` (113); `#expHeadTpl` (228) and `#expBulletTpl` (63) are one atom family and should be weighed together rather than split. Decide granularity - seven components or grouped - against this pilot rather than in advance, and carry each block's own rules out of `cv-preview.component.scss` with it.
- **Evidence:** ADR-0005 amendment sixty-three.

**What actually happened.** Splitting `onboarding-content.util.ts` at the targeting seam was the last
code change in the session, forced by the size gate. After it I re-ran `desktop:type-check` and
`quality:file-size` and **not the suites** - and type-check cannot see this class of error, because

`formatCompRange`, `normalizeCurrency` and `parseArchetypesSkillResponse` from the file they had just
left. **CI found it, not the local gate set** - twelve failures in `application`, fixed in `d4fd0c6`

`desktop` 1417/1417 on the merged tree, with the full gate set green in CI.

**The rule this is worth writing down:** a change made _after_ the gate set has run invalidates the
gate set, not just the file it touched. The split was the fourth change of its kind in this campaign
to be forced by a gate late in a session, so the sequencing is predictable rather than unlucky - the
suites belong after the last edit, not after the last edit I judged to be risky.

and did not reproduce on re-run or in CI. It is unrelated to this work and flaky; recorded rather than

  deleted in the same call. Happy paths: a market pick persists and offers its source plan; a region

  empty; the key save trims and clears the draft with the field reading empty; remove flips the
  button count and `canTest`; CLI mode probes and draws both status rows; the custom model choice
  opens the free-text field **without** writing `__custom__` into the row. Then with the stub made to
  throw: a failed reset **closed the confirmation** instead of leaving an armed dialog, a failed save
  released `saving`, and a failed geo toggle rolled the record back to exactly its previous value.
  All three toasted. Part one's `<ng-content>` order and 16px `:host` gaps still measure right.

  "no" rather than leaving the previous provider's answer standing, which would unlock a Test button
  that can only fail. Six tests pin this, one of which asserts the public surface has no getter. No
  new IPC command, no new storage, no new external call.

     so the settings row has one copy rather than two that can disagree.
  3. `refused` kept apart from `failed` for CLI installs; the model picker answers `null` for the
     custom choice rather than returning the sentinel.

  first run asserting `geoScope: 'europe'` where the encoder produces `'["europe"]'`. Fixed by
  asserting against `encodeGeoScopes` rather than writing the literal - a hardcoded encoding is a
  second implementation of it, and it would have passed while disagreeing with the real one.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none intended. Every behaviour is the same screen; the reset,
  save and geo rollback paths were each exercised in the browser.

### 2026-08-09, GA4 had never received a hit, and every visible sign said it had

- **Status:** complete
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code (Opus 5; triaged 4/10 for the investigation, re-triaged 5/10 for fix + test + deploy - radius 1, ambiguity 0, risk 2, verify 2, unknowns 0. Risk 2 because deployment is outward-facing. No subagents, no gate; the cause was measured rather than argued.)
- **Branch:** `fix/ga4-datalayer-arguments`
- **Commits:** `50ef823` (the fix and its tests), `b0e6cb1` (sitemap `lastmod` refreshed by the production build)
- **Pull request:** [#387](https://github.com/vitala89/applye/pull/387), MERGEABLE. Its checks were queued at the time of writing; GitHub Actions on this repository fails within seconds on billing, which is why the deployment was manual.
- **Objective:** answer whether applye.dev's empty GA4 property was a deliberate configuration or a fault, then fix it if it was a fault.

- **The answer was a fault, in the code, and it had cost every hit since launch.** `AnalyticsService.load()` installed its shim as `(...args) => win.dataLayer?.push(args)`, pushing a plain array per command. gtag.js reads a queued command **only** as an `arguments` object and ignores anything else without a warning, so `js` and `config` never executed, no destination was configured, and no `/g/collect` request ever left the page.

- **Why no instrument in this repository could have caught it.** The bundle was correct, the ID was correct, consent worked, and the script loaded: `window.gtag` was a function, `window.google_tag_manager['G-ZY158GV42C']` existed (it is created from the script's own URL, not from `config`, so it proves nothing), and `dataLayer` grew to five entries. Nothing threw, no CSP existed to violate, and GA4's only report was "data collection isn't active on your website" - which reads as a missing tag rather than a present and mute one.

- **Measured, not reasoned.** On the live site with consent granted: zero requests matching `/collect/` in `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')`. Then, on the same page, a canonical `function g(){dataLayer.push(arguments)}` plus `js`, `config` and one event produced a `region1.google-analytics.com/g/collect?...&tid=G-ZY158GV42C` hit within two seconds. That isolated the fault to the shim and cleared GA4, the network, consent and the property configuration in one step. Connectivity to `google-analytics.com` was confirmed separately with a `no-cors` fetch, so a blocked host was ruled out before the probe.

- **Completed:**
  - The shim is an exported `installGtag(win)` that pushes `arguments`. Exporting it is what makes it testable: the service's own `load()` is unreachable from unit tests because the committed measurement ID is the placeholder that keeps checkouts out of the real property.
  - Four tests: the queued value is `[object Arguments]` and not an array, its contents survive intact, an existing `dataLayer` is reused rather than replaced, and the shim is published on the window.
  - **The first test was proved to fail against the old shape** - `push(Array.from(arguments))` was substituted deliberately, the suite went to 1 failed / 79 passed, and the file was restored.
  - `prefer-rest-params` is disabled on exactly that line, with the reason above it, because obeying the rule is the bug. The redundant second disable that ESLint flagged was removed.
  - Docs: `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased/Fixed; `docs/internal/ANALYTICS_SETUP.md` gains a "When the tag is present and the property is still empty" section with the thirty-second `performance` check and the canonical probe, and its status block and stale "nothing is deployed" item are corrected.

- **Not completed:** nothing. The branch is pushed and #387 is open; only the merge itself is outstanding.

- **Files changed:** `apps/web/src/app/analytics/analytics.service.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/analytics/analytics.spec.ts`, `apps/web/public/sitemap.xml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/internal/ANALYTICS_SETUP.md`.

- **Validation:** `nx run web:test` 80/80 passing across 6 suites; `nx run web:lint` clean, 0 errors and 0 warnings after the redundant disable came out; `npm run format:check` passed; `git diff --check` clean; `npm run quality:file-size` and `npm run quality:attribution` both passed. The desktop suites were not run - nothing outside `apps/web` was touched.

- **Deployed and verified on the live site.** `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID=G-ZY158GV42C npm run web:build`, then `wrangler pages deploy dist/apps/web/browser --project-name=applye --branch=main`, 105 files, deployment `e29e87e0`. `deploy.sh` was bypassed because it requires `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` in the environment while wrangler here is authenticated by OAuth; every gate the script runs had already been run by hand. The placeholder was restored with `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID= npm run web:analytics-config` immediately afterwards, and the working tree confirms `G-PLACEHOLDER`. On the deployed bundle, after accepting consent: `dataLayer` holds `[object Arguments]` entries, and a `region1.google-analytics.com/g/collect?v=2&tid=G-ZY158GV42C` hit is present.

- **One transient 404 during the rollout, not a defect.** `chunk-2XV5VSJU.js` returned 404 to the browser in the seconds after upload while `main-SQRE4SI3.js` already served, so that one page load could not bootstrap. Both the apex and the `*.pages.dev` deployment URL returned 200 immediately afterwards and the next load was clean. Worth knowing before diagnosing it as a broken build: a direct-upload Pages deploy is briefly inconsistent across edge nodes.

- **Privacy/security impact:** none by design, and worth stating precisely - the consent gate, the `sanitiseParams` allow list, IP anonymisation and both ad-signal switches are untouched. The change makes the already-declared collection actually happen; it widens nothing. What visitors were told the site collects is now what it collects.

- **Decisions and assumptions:** the shim was exported rather than tested through the service, because reaching `load()` would mean shipping a real measurement ID into the test environment - the exact thing the placeholder arrangement exists to prevent. Deployment went ahead on the maintainer's explicit instruction.

- **Risks:** GA4 needs up to 48 hours to stop reporting "data collection isn't active", so the property will look unchanged for a while after a correct fix. Absolute numbers will stay below real traffic because the consent gate makes decliners invisible - by design, recorded in `ANALYTICS_SETUP.md`.

- **Open issues:** three diagnostic events were sent to the production property while proving the cause - `claude_probe_cfg` landed, and `claude_probe_array` / `claude_probe_args` did not because they hit the broken path. They will appear in reports for that day and are not real traffic.

- **Next first action:** merge #387, so `main` carries what is already live. Then, once hits accumulate for a day: mark `download_click` as a key event, and define internal traffic plus switch that filter from Testing to **Active** - both were blocked on traffic that until now did not exist.

- **Evidence:** `50ef823`, `b0e6cb1`; deployment `e29e87e0.applye.pages.dev`; the live `/g/collect` hit quoted above.

- **Open issues or blockers:** none.
- **Lessons:**
  - **Deleting an allowlist entry is a claim that has to be tested from the other side.** Lint passing after the deletion only proves the rule found nothing; it does not prove the rule would have. Re-adding the injection and watching it fail costs one minute and is the only thing that distinguishes "migrated" from "silently unmatched" - which is exactly how the first version of this allowlist failed, with repo-relative paths that matched nothing.
  - **An extraction is the moment a latent identity bug becomes visible.** `pullFromProfile`'s in-place assignment had been there all along and worked by accident of which reference the template compared. Writing it as a pure function forced the question that reading it never had.
  - **A private helper shared by two callers can quietly add a round trip.** Factoring the render-and-run out of both AI paths, the first version read `getSettings` inside the helper while both callers had already read it. Cheap to miss, and only a call-count assertion catches it.

It is covered by nine store tests plus the record module's own, including the sibling-displacement ordering (siblings first, then this row) and the failure path leaving `saving` clear.

  - **A mutation test is only as good as the asymmetry in its fixtures.** Two live guards in `moveCvSection` survived deletion with all 46 tests green, because every fixture was already pinned and reindexed - the normal form the function itself produces - so refusing and falling through agreed on all of them. On a drifted list they differ: refusing returns it verbatim, falling through reindexes it. Nearly deleted both as dead code on the strength of the green run.
  - **A surviving mutant is a claim about the tests, not yet a verdict on the code.** The first reading here - "the guard is unreachable, `reorderCvSections` re-pins anyway" - was coherent, specific, and wrong. Worth asking what input would make the branch observable before concluding it cannot be.
  - **One guard can mask another.** After adding drifted-list cases, the locked-key check still survived: the case moved `photo`, whose neighbour is also locked, so the neighbour check refused first. It took moving `personal_details` down onto `summary` to isolate it. When two checks can refuse the same call, at least one case has to reach each of them alone.
- **Next first action:** `CvRegenerationStore`, fourth and last on `cv-detail` (589/400): `regenerateSection` and `pullFromProfile`, roughly 90 lines of prompt assembly and AI calls, injecting `DbService` and `AiService`.   - **ADR-0005 amendment five** records the reversal and the general rule it produced.
- **Not completed:** nothing in scope. `COMPONENTS_STILL_USING_THE_GATEWAY` still holds 26 entries by design - the page keeps `inject(DbService)` for the document cluster until PR 3.
- **Files or packages changed:** `apps/desktop/.../cv-detail.component.ts`, `apps/desktop/.../cv-style-scope.util.ts` (+ spec, new), `libs/application/src/lib/documents/cv-style.store.ts` (+ spec, new), `libs/application/src/index.ts`, `docs/product/decisions/ADR-0005-application-layer-owns-page-state.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, this log.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check`; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop,application --skip-nx-cache` (0 errors, 8 warnings - all pre-existing `no-non-null-assertion`); `nx run-many --target=test --skip-nx-cache` (7 projects, desktop 118 suites/1421 tests, application 10/140); `nx build desktop`; `npm run quality:file-size` (passed; `cv-detail.component.ts` 709/400, base 962); `npm run quality:attribution`; `npx nx format:check`; `git diff --check`. **Mutation testing:** four mutations per new module, each asserted to match exactly once before applying and each file diffed back byte-exact afterwards - all eight killed.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. No new I/O; the one gateway call moved unchanged.
- **Decisions and assumptions:**
  - **The cascade does not go to `libs/core`, reversing amendment four.** Its only input is `CvStylePanelChange`, one widget's wire format, which amendment two's "domain or format" test puts on the format side. The move would have exported that type plus `CvPreviewSelection` as core public API and churned nine `apps/desktop` import sites.
  - **`cv-style.util.ts` does not move.** It is already pure, imports only `@applye/core`, and also serves the cover-letter editor. The alternative was moving cover-letter helpers into a CV directory, or splitting a module whose own header states why its functions belong together.
  - **A store owns state, not necessarily the code that edits it.** `type:application` may not import from the app, so `CvStyleStore` cannot call the app-local helpers; the page composes the next style and commits it through `applyStyle`. Page geometry stayed on the page for the same reason - `resolvePageSettings` is app-local.
  - **The save-template trio moves to `CvDocumentStore`, not here.** It never reads `style`; it writes `cvTemplateUpsert` from sections, region tag and the photo flags.
  - **`styleOpen` and `styleNoteMessage` stay page state** - a collapse toggle and a translation lookup, the same shape as `livePanelOpen` and `collapsedSections`.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none observed. Every write path funnels through `applyStyle`, preserving the previous debounce timing exactly; `selectTheme` and `resetAllStyles` still check immediately and still cancel a pending debounced check, which is one of the mutations tested.
- **Open issues or blockers:** none.
- **Lessons:**
  - **A decision recorded in an ADR can still be wrong, and the gate that catches it is reading the code before writing it.** Amendment four named the file to create and the test that justified it. The test was right; its application was not, and only the actual signatures showed that.
  - **Check the dependency direction before assigning code to a layer.** The `libs/core` question looked settled until `type:application`'s allowlist made the follow-on obvious: a store in `libs/application` cannot reach a helper in `apps/desktop`. That constraint - not the domain/format test - is what forced the final shape, and it was invisible from the line count the plan was built on.
  - **The page shrinks by the same amount wherever the pure module lives.** Worth saying out loud during a size-driven migration, because it removes the pressure to promote code to a library just to make a number move.
- **Next first action:** `CvDocumentStore`, third of four PRs on `cv-detail` (709/400): load, save, sections, reorder, lock, and the save-template trio. It injects `CvStyleStore` and `CvPhotoStore` to assemble the single `documentLibraryUpsert` write, and its landing is what deletes `cv-detail.component.ts` from `COMPONENTS_STILL_USING_THE_GATEWAY`.

Outside the repository: the global skill and hook.

The skill was invoked live and produced a verdict (7/10) on the next real task. `npx nx format:check`, `git diff --check`, `npm run quality:attribution`. **Not run:** `quality:file-size` has no source files to check, and no test, lint or build target covers `.claude/` or `~/.claude/`.

Open `/hooks` once, or restart, and the next prompt will carry the reminder.

  - **`**/` inside a `/** */` block comment ends the comment** - hit yesterday in `eslint.config.mjs`, avoided today by writing "double-star glob" in prose.

### 2026-08-06, the boundary gets a lint rule, and the migration order turns out to be inverted

- **Status:** complete
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code (Opus 5)
- **Branch:** `feat/component-gateway-lint-rule`
- **Commits:** one
- **Pull request:** opened against `main`
- **Objective:** pick the next page after Discover. The answer was that the ranking was wrong and the enforcement mechanism did not exist.
- **Completed:**
  - **`eslint.config.mjs` gains a `no-restricted-syntax` error over `*.component.ts`** for `inject(DbService)`, with `COMPONENTS_STILL_USING_THE_GATEWAY` listing the 26 components that still do. The list only shrinks. Verified both directions, under `nx lint` and directly.
  - **ADR-0005 amendment four**, recording three corrections: the enforcement mechanism, the deferral of `jobs`, and the migration order by dependency shape rather than line count. Plus `cv-detail`'s three-store decomposition and the `libs/core` `cv/` gate for the `CvStyle` cascade rules.
  - Propagated to `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENT_START_HERE.md`, `CODE_QUALITY.md` - all four said "lint does not enforce it yet", which is now false.
- **Not completed:** no page migrated in this branch; it is governance only. `cv-detail`'s three stores are next, one per PR.
- **Files or packages changed:** `eslint.config.mjs`, `ADR-0005`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/internal/AGENT_START_HERE.md`, `docs/governance/CODE_QUALITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`, this log.
- **Validation:** `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop,application --skip-nx-cache` (clean, and failing as designed on an injected violation); `nx run desktop:type-check`; `nx run-many --target=test`; `nx build desktop`; `npm run quality:file-size`; `npm run quality:attribution`; `npx nx format:check`; `git diff --check`.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. Lint configuration and documentation.
- **Decisions and assumptions:**
  - **The allowlist flip was never the rule the ADR described.** `depConstraints` is per project tag, so it cannot say "components only". The component rule is separate, is an error now, and the flip stays as a later goal that also requires moving the app's `shared/*` services.
  - **`jobs` is deferred, and the reason is written down.** 1050 lines, but **9** gateway calls against **22** app-service injections across 150-odd use sites. A store in `libs/application` cannot inject an app service, so the page cannot move until those services do - and five of them are 251-326 lines and must decompose first.
  - **`cv-detail` is next** (1019 lines, 14 gateway calls, 1 app service), then `tracker` and `cover-letter-detail` which share its shape.
  - **`cv-preview` (1049) and `cv-live-style-panel` (704) reach the gateway zero times**, so this campaign does not touch them at all. Their size is view state.
  - `cv-detail` becomes `CvDocumentStore`, `CvStyleStore`, `CvPhotoStore`; preview/live-selection and return-to-wizard routing stay page state; the `CvStyle` cascade rules become `libs/core/.../cv/`.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none at runtime. The risk was a rule that silently matches nothing, which is why it was tested from both sides.
- **Open issues or blockers:** none.
- **Lessons, each of which cost something:**
  - **A `files` pattern in a spread config resolves against the config that was loaded, not the file that declares it.** `nx lint` loads `apps/desktop/eslint.config.mjs`, which spreads the root config, so `apps/desktop/src/...` in the allowlist matched **nothing** - meaning the rule would have errored on all 26 files under nx while looking correct at the root. Double-star globs match under both base paths. Found by testing the allowlist rather than trusting a green run.
  - **A green lint run is not proof the rule works.** The first "all 26 silent" check returned zero matches because **ESLint had crashed**, and `grep -c` on a stack trace is also zero. Assert the mechanism, not the absence of output.
  - **`**/` inside a `/** */` block comment ends the comment.** A sentence explaining the glob form broke the whole config, and node reported it as `Unexpected identifier 'nx'` on line 1 - pointing at the import, 20 lines from the actual cause. If a config suddenly fails to parse at line 1, look for a comment that closed itself.
  - **Ranking work by the number the ratchet reports can invert the real order.** `jobs` is the worst class in the repository and the worst candidate for this migration; two of the biggest files in the campaign (`cv-preview`, `cv-live-style-panel`) touch the gateway zero times and are outside it entirely. One `grep -c` per page settled all of it, and it should have been run eight sessions ago.
- **Next first action:** `CvDocumentStore` - the document itself (load, save, sections, reorder, lock, regenerate, pull-from-profile) out of `cv-detail.component.ts` (1019/400), and its line deleted from `COMPONENTS_STILL_USING_THE_GATEWAY` only when the file no longer injects `DbService` at all, which will take all three stores.

### 2026-08-06, the layer never notifies, and Discover leaves the gateway

- **Status:** complete
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code (Opus 5)
- **Branch:** `feat/discover-sources-store`
- **Commits:** one
- **Pull request:** opened against `main`
- **Objective:** answer Step 1b - what happens to a service that both reaches the gateway and toasts - and apply the answer to `DiscoverSourcesService`, the last file under `pages/discover/` injecting `DbService`.
- **Completed:**
  - **Grilling gate, two rounds, six questions.** ADR-0005 has a third amendment: **nothing in `libs/application` notifies the user.** A member returns its outcome; the component decides whether and how to say it. Rejected: a notification port on the layer, moving `ToastService` into a library, and a rule that notifying services stay in the app (which would leave the allowlist flip permanently open).
  - `discover-sources.service.ts` (173) -> `libs/application/.../discover-sources.store.ts` (**168** non-empty, budget 250), with `resultLine` and `formatScanTime` on the `scan-console.ts` precedent. `discover-sources.util.ts` (68) moved whole; the page and drawer import `toggled` and `narrowBuiltinsByMarkets` back through the barrel.
  - The four writes return `{ ok: boolean; error?: string }`. The drawer raises all seven notifications, because it already owned all four call sites - the page needed no change beyond its imports.
  - **`grep inject(DbService)`: 45 -> 44.** No file under `pages/discover/` reaches the gateway.
  - `discover.component.ts` **618 -> 618**; see the ratchet note below for why that number is not an accident.
  - Tests: store spec 13 (was 11 as a service spec), new drawer spec 7, **1392 desktop + 98 application, all passing**. Six mutations, six killed.
- **Not completed:** the three other notifying services (`job-actions` 4 toasts, `portal-answers` 2, `cover-letter-tailor` 1) convert with their own pages, by the scope decision.
- **Files or packages changed:** `libs/application` (store, util, two specs, barrel), `apps/desktop` Discover page and Sources drawer (+ new drawer spec), `CHANGELOG.md`, `ADR-0005`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`, this log.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check`; `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop,application --skip-nx-cache`; `nx run-many --target=test --projects=desktop,application --skip-nx-cache`; `nx build desktop`; `npm run quality:file-size`; `npm run quality:attribution`; `npx nx format:check`; `git diff --check`. **`quality:style-move` was deliberately not run:** no stylesheet changed in this branch, so there was no move to prove.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none. Orchestration moved between files in the same process; no storage, network or `invoke` behaviour changed.
- **Decisions and assumptions:**
  - **The layer never notifies** (ADR-0005 amendment three). The `type:data` allowlist flip stays the end goal.
  - **Two failure shapes, chosen by whether refusal is possible.** `string | null` stays right for a write that either works or fails; a write that can refuse its own empty input needs three outcomes, because `null` would mean both "created" and "nothing to do" and the drawer would clear a form the user was still filling in.
  - **The 250-line budget matches every file in `libs/application`, not only `*.store.ts`.** Five services that must eventually move are 251-326 lines, so they decompose when they move. This is a planning fact for `jobs` and the CV pages.
  - Scope: rule decided now, applied to Discover only.
- **Risks or compatibility impact:** none functional. The seven messages are raised from one component instead of one service, with the same keys and the same conditions.
- **Open issues or blockers:** none for this branch.
- **Lessons, each of which cost something:**
  - **A directive left behind is the host-element trap one layer up, and it is completely silent.** The drawer's markup carries `<a routerLink="/settings">`, but `RouterLink` stayed in the **page's** `imports` when that markup moved into the child. Without the directive the attribute is literal - no `href`, no navigation - and `routerLink` is a valid attribute name, so type-check, lint, the build and 1391 tests all passed on a dead link. The only hint was a compiler **warning** about the page's now-unused import, which says nothing about the drawer. It was found by chasing the ratchet, not by looking for it. **Every past extraction should be re-checked for directives, not only for CSS rules**: `RouterLink`, `FormsModule`/`ngModel`, and any structural directive whose markup crossed a component boundary.
  - **The handoff's framing was wrong, and it was cheap to check.** "The shape of the last mile on every page" was **4 of 19** services: 15 of the gateway-using services notify nothing. One `grep -c` per file, before the interview, and it changed which options were worth asking about.
  - **The ratchet paid for itself again.** Replacing two single-line imports with three entries in a braced block is **+1 line**, and the ratchet refused the branch at 619/618. The fix was not cosmetic: the dead `RouterLink` entry was the line to remove, and removing it is what surfaced the bug above.
  - **A real `TranslateService` in a spec resolves keys to English copy.** Asserting `'discover.source_added'` against `'Source added.'` fails; the store spec's stub (`{ t: () => (k) => k }`) is what keeps the assertion about _which_ message is raised rather than about the wording.
  - **`grep -cF` on a multiline pattern counts matching lines, not matches.** A mutation asserting "exactly one" saw 5 and refused to apply - correctly, and only because the assertion was there. Re-run with `perl -0777` and a substitution count, which is the thing actually being asserted.

### 2026-08-06, Discover's deterministic scoring leaves the page, and two of its own comments turn out to be wrong

- **Status:** complete
- **Agent/tool:** Claude Code (Opus 5)
- **Branch:** `refactor/discover-detail-scoring`
- **Completed:** `discover-detail-scoring.ts` owns `SKILL_DICT` (45 names), `detectSkills` and `computeRawScore`. Class **802 -> 730**. Suite **1442 -> 1459**.
- **Why this seam.** It is the zero-token half of the detail screen - what the user sees before asking for anything - and it had **no tests at all**. Same shape as the location-tree cut: pure logic that was only ever exercised through a page.
- **Not in `libs/`**, for the third time and the same reason: nothing outside this page needs it, and a `libs/` public API change goes through the grilling gate rather than riding a refactor.
- **Validation:** `nx run desktop:type-check`, `nx run-many --target=lint --projects=desktop` (0 errors; 8 pre-existing warnings elsewhere), `nx test desktop` (**1459 passing**), `nx build desktop`, `npm run quality:file-size` (730 against base 802), `npm run quality:attribution`, `npx nx format:check`, `git diff --check`. `quality:style-move` does not apply: no stylesheet changed.
- **Backwards diff.** `detectSkills` reproduces token-for-token, and all 45 `SKILL_DICT` entries are byte-identical. **`computeRawScore` does not, deliberately**: its three signal reads (`profileKeywords`, `detailSkills`, and the open row's archetype through `archetypeBadge`) became arguments, and its inline tier table is a named `TIER_BOOST`. That makes visible an ordering dependency the method hid - the skills must be detected before the score is computed, or the bonus is taken from the previous job. The call site now passes `skills` as a local, so the order is in the code rather than in the reader's head.
- **Mutation testing: eight written, eight killed.** The whole-word cutoff moving by one character; eleven skills where the chips fit ten; ordinary names matching case-sensitively; coverage dividing by every keyword rather than the first ten; a detected skill worth four rather than three; a secondary archetype boosted like a primary one; an empty profile scoring zero instead of declining to score; coverage worth 50 points rather than 55. Each asserts its pattern matched exactly once before applying; restore verified byte-identical.
- **Two of the code's own comments were wrong, and writing the tests is what found them.**
  - "Coverage saturates at ten keywords" - the **denominator** saturates, the numerator does not. With twenty keywords, matching all twenty gives a coverage of 2.0 and a formula score of 140. Only the ceiling bounds it. Harmless, and arguably right (matching twenty of your keywords _is_ a strong match), but it is not what the comment said.
  - The clamp is written `Math.max(20, Math.min(97, score))`, and **the floor is unreachable**: the formula starts at 30 and every other term is non-negative. A test asserting `>= 20` would have been vacuous, so the test pins **30** - the floor that actually occurs - and fails if the base or any term changes such that it could drop.
- **Two of my own test expectations were wrong first, and the code was right.** Dictionary order put `Go` before `C#`, and the coverage assertion assumed the saturation the comment claimed. Both were corrected against the code rather than the code against them.
- **Privacy/security impact:** none.
- **Next first action:** `discover.component.ts` is 730/400. The two remaining candidates are unaudited: the **scan pipeline** (`scan`, the console lines, the per-source results - the more I/O-shaped) and the **detail loading path** (`openDetail`, `loadDetail`, `detailBlocks`, `detailSalary` - the more self-contained, and a candidate for a component-scoped service; see the standing follow-up about component-scoped services outliving their page).
